pull-up.title: Pull-Up
pull-up.about: A bodyweight vertical pull that builds wide lats and a strong upper back with a big overhead stretch.
steps: Hang from the bar with arms fully straight and shoulders stretched.
Brace your core and keep legs still.
Drive elbows down toward your ribs until your chin clears the bar.
Lower slowly back to a full dead hang.
cues: Think elbows to back pockets, not hands to bar.
Start every rep from a full stretch.
Keep chest up and lean back slightly.

mistakes.text: Kipping or swinging to cheat reps.
mistakes.fix: Brace your core, keep legs still and pull with your back only.

mistakes.text: Stopping short of a full hang at the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly back to a full dead hang before every rep.

assisted-pull-up.title: Assisted Pull-Up
assisted-pull-up.about: A machine-assisted pull-up that lets you train the full lat range with adjustable load.
steps: Set the counterweight and kneel or stand on the pad.
Grip the handles and let arms straighten fully overhead.
Pull elbows down and in until your chin passes the handles.
Control the way up into a deep lat stretch.
cues: Use only enough assistance to reach near failure in your rep range.
Keep shoulders down at the top of the pull.
Pause briefly in the stretched position.

mistakes.text: Using so much assistance the set becomes easy.
mistakes.fix: Use only enough assistance to reach near failure in your rep range.

mistakes.text: Bouncing out of the bottom instead of controlling it.
mistakes.fix: Control the way up and pause briefly in the stretched position.

bench-assisted-pull-up.title: Bench-Assisted Pull-Up
bench-assisted-pull-up.about: A home-gym pull-up where your feet on a bench provide just enough help to finish hard reps.
steps: Place a bench behind a bar and rest your feet on it.
Hang with straight arms and hips slightly bent.
Pull your chest toward the bar using your back first.
Use your legs only as much as needed to finish the rep.
Lower slowly to a full stretch.
cues: Let the back do most of the work.
Reduce leg help as you get stronger.
Keep a full hang at the bottom.

mistakes.text: Turning it into a leg press with the arms along.
mistakes.fix: Pull with your back first and use your legs only to finish the rep.

mistakes.text: Cutting the bottom range short.
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly to a full hang with straight arms each rep.

lat-pulldown.title: Lat Pulldown
lat-pulldown.about: A cable vertical pull that loads the lats through a long, stable range and is easy to progress.
steps: Lock your thighs under the pad and grip the bar.
Let the weight stretch your arms fully overhead.
Pull the bar to your upper chest, driving elbows down.
Return slowly until your lats are fully stretched.
cues: Lead with the elbows, keep hands as hooks.
Lean back only slightly; keep the torso steady.
Control the eccentric for two to three seconds.

mistakes.text: Leaning far back and turning it into a row.
mistakes.fix: Lean back only slightly and pull the bar to your upper chest.

mistakes.text: Letting the stack yank you up without control.
mistakes.fix: Control the return for two to three seconds into a full stretch.

close-grip-pulldown.title: Close-Grip Pulldown
close-grip-pulldown.about: A neutral, close-grip pulldown that keeps elbows tight to the body for strong lat emphasis.
steps: Attach a V-bar or two handles and sit under the pad.
Reach up and let your shoulders rise into a full stretch.
Pull handles to your upper chest, elbows tracking close to your sides.
Return under control to the full overhead stretch.
cues: Drive elbows down toward your hips.
Keep a slight lean and a proud chest.
Own the stretch at the top of every rep.

mistakes.text: Pulling with the arms and shrugging the shoulders.
mistakes.fix: Drive your elbows down toward your hips and keep shoulders down.

mistakes.text: Short reps that skip the stretch.
mistakes.fix: Return to the full overhead stretch at the top of every rep.

dumbbell-pullover.title: Dumbbell Pullover
dumbbell-pullover.about: A shoulder-extension movement that trains the lats in a deep overhead stretch without biceps fatigue.
steps: Lie on a bench holding one dumbbell over your chest.
Keep elbows slightly bent and fixed.
Lower the weight behind your head until lats and chest stretch.
Pull it back over your chest using your lats.
cues: Keep ribs down so the lower back does not arch.
Move only at the shoulder, not the elbows.
Stop the top just before tension disappears.

mistakes.text: Bending the elbows and turning it into a triceps extension.
mistakes.fix: Keep elbows slightly bent and fixed; move only at the shoulder.

mistakes.text: Flaring the ribs and arching hard to fake range.
mistakes.fix: Keep ribs down and stop where your lower back would start to arch.

barbell-pullover.title: Barbell Pullover
barbell-pullover.about: A pullover with a bar that allows heavier loading of the lats in a long stretched position.
steps: Lie on a flat or slightly inclined bench with a bar over your chest.
Use a shoulder-width grip and soft elbows.
Arc the bar back behind your head into a deep stretch.
Sweep it back over your chest with your lats.
cues: Keep elbow angle constant throughout.
Brace your core to keep the lower back flat.
Go slow through the bottom stretch.

mistakes.text: Letting the elbows flare and bend.
mistakes.fix: Keep a soft, constant elbow angle throughout the movement.

mistakes.text: Dropping the bar too fast into the stretch.
mistakes.fix: Lower the bar slowly through the bottom stretch.

cable-pullover.title: Cable Pullover
cable-pullover.about: A straight-arm cable pull that keeps constant tension on the lats from stretch to contraction.
steps: Set a cable high and grab a bar, rope or handle.
Hinge slightly and reach arms up into a stretch.
With soft elbows, sweep your hands down to your thighs.
Let the cable pull your arms back up slowly.
cues: Think about pulling with your armpits.
Keep elbows locked at a slight bend.
Reach fully overhead on every rep.

mistakes.text: Bending elbows and pushing down like a triceps pressdown.
mistakes.fix: Keep elbows locked at a slight bend and pull with your armpits.

mistakes.text: Rocking the torso to move the weight.
mistakes.fix: Hold a slight hinge and move only your arms.

barbell-row.title: Barbell Row
barbell-row.about: A heavy bent-over row that builds overall back thickness and is easy to overload.
steps: Hinge forward with a flat back, bar hanging at arm's length.
Brace your core and keep knees softly bent.
Row the bar to your lower ribs, squeezing shoulder blades.
Lower slowly until arms and shoulders are fully stretched.
cues: Keep torso angle fixed; don't stand up as you pull.
Pull with elbows, not wrists.
Let shoulder blades spread at the bottom.

mistakes.text: Using hip drive and momentum on every rep.
mistakes.fix: Keep your torso angle fixed and row with your arms and back only.

mistakes.text: Rounding the lower back under load.
mistakes.fix: Brace your core and keep a flat back on every rep.

pendlay-row.title: Pendlay Row
pendlay-row.about: A strict row from a dead stop on the floor that builds explosive back strength without momentum.
steps: Set the bar on the floor and hinge until your torso is near parallel.
Grip just outside shoulder width with a flat back.
Pull the bar explosively to your upper stomach.
Return it to the floor and reset each rep.
cues: Keep the torso still; only the arms and shoulder blades move.
Start each rep from a full arm stretch.
Brace hard before every pull.

mistakes.text: Raising the chest to meet the bar.
mistakes.fix: Keep the torso still; move only the arms and shoulder blades.

mistakes.text: Bouncing the bar off the floor.
mistakes.fix: Set the bar down on the floor and reset before each pull.

dumbbell-row-bent-over.title: Bent-Over Dumbbell Row
dumbbell-row-bent-over.about: A two-dumbbell bent-over row that lets each arm move freely for a long range and deep stretch.
steps: Hold two dumbbells and hinge until your torso is near parallel.
Let the weights hang straight below your shoulders.
Row both dumbbells toward your hips.
Lower slowly and let your shoulder blades stretch forward.
cues: Keep a neutral spine and fixed torso angle.
Drive elbows back, not just up.
Use the extra range dumbbells give you.

mistakes.text: Standing more upright as you fatigue.
mistakes.fix: Keep a fixed torso angle, near parallel, for the whole set.

mistakes.text: Jerking the weights up with momentum.
mistakes.fix: Row the dumbbells smoothly toward your hips and lower slowly.

one-arm-dumbbell-row.title: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
one-arm-dumbbell-row.about: A supported single-arm row that gives a huge lat stretch and lets you focus on one side.
steps: Brace one hand on a bench or your knee with a flat back.
Let the dumbbell hang and your shoulder drop into a stretch.
Pull the dumbbell toward your hip, elbow close to your side.
Lower slowly until the lat is fully lengthened.
cues: Pull in an arc toward the hip for more lats.
Keep hips and shoulders square; avoid twisting.
Pause briefly in the bottom stretch.

mistakes.text: Rotating the torso to heave the weight.
mistakes.fix: Keep hips and shoulders square and pull in an arc toward the hip.

mistakes.text: Shrugging the dumbbell up toward the ear.
mistakes.fix: Pull the dumbbell toward your hip with the elbow close to your side.

one-arm-lat-row.title: Single-Arm Lat Row
one-arm-lat-row.about: A one-arm row path aimed at the lats, pulling low toward the hip from a deep reach.
steps: Set up supported with your working arm reaching forward.
Let the shoulder reach long for a full lat stretch.
Pull the handle down and back toward your hip.
Return slowly to the long reach.
cues: Keep the elbow tucked close to your side.
Think of moving the elbow, not curling the hand.
Stop when the elbow reaches your torso.

mistakes.text: Flaring the elbow high, shifting work to the upper back.
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbow tucked close to your side as you pull.

mistakes.text: Cutting off the forward stretch.
mistakes.fix: Return slowly to the long reach so the lat fully stretches.

high-elbow-dumbbell-row.title: High-Elbow Dumbbell Row
high-elbow-dumbbell-row.about: A row with elbows flared wide that shifts work to the upper back, mid traps and rear delts.
steps: Hinge or brace on a support with the dumbbell hanging.
Turn the elbow out about 60–90 degrees from your torso.
Row the elbow up and back toward your shoulder line.
Lower slowly and let the shoulder blade spread.
cues: Lead with the elbow, keep the wrist relaxed.
Squeeze shoulder blades together at the top.
Get a full stretch across the upper back at the bottom.

mistakes.text: Shrugging up into the neck instead of pulling back.
mistakes.fix: Row the elbow back toward your shoulder line and squeeze the blades.

mistakes.text: Tucking the elbow, which turns it into a lat row.
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbow turned out about 60–90 degrees from your torso.

chest-supported-row.title: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
chest-supported-row.about: An incline-bench row that removes lower-back fatigue so all effort goes into the back.
steps: Lie chest-down on an incline bench with dumbbells hanging.
Let your shoulders sink forward into a stretch.
Row the dumbbells back toward your hips or lower ribs.
Lower slowly to a full hang.
cues: Keep your chest glued to the pad.
Choose elbow angle to bias lats (tucked) or upper back (flared).
Control every eccentric.

mistakes.text: Lifting the chest off the bench to cheat.
mistakes.fix: Keep your chest glued to the pad for every rep.

mistakes.text: Short reps without a full stretch.
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly to a full hang and let your shoulders sink forward.

chest-supported-high-elbow-row.title: Chest-Supported High-Elbow Row
chest-supported-high-elbow-row.about: A supported row with flared elbows that isolates the upper back and rear delts without lower-back strain.
steps: Lie chest-down on an incline or flat bench.
Hang the dumbbells with palms facing back or down.
Row with elbows flared wide toward shoulder height.
Lower slowly until shoulder blades fully protract.
cues: Keep the chest pinned to the pad.
Pull elbows back, not hands up.
Squeeze the upper back for a beat at the top.

mistakes.text: Shrugging toward the ears.
mistakes.fix: Pull your elbows back, not up, and keep shoulders away from ears.

mistakes.text: Letting the weights drop without control.
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly until your shoulder blades fully spread.

bodyweight-row.title: Bodyweight Row
bodyweight-row.about: An inverted row under a bar or table that trains the upper back with zero equipment cost.
steps: Lie under a sturdy bar or table edge and grab it.
Keep your body straight from heels to head.
Pull your chest up, elbows flared for upper back.
Lower slowly to straight arms.
cues: Squeeze glutes and abs to stay rigid.
Walk feet forward to make it harder.
Touch the bar or get close each rep.

mistakes.text: Sagging the hips toward the floor.
mistakes.fix: Squeeze glutes and abs to keep a straight line from heels to head.

mistakes.text: Craning the neck forward to fake range.
mistakes.fix: Keep your neck neutral and pull your chest toward the bar.

t-bar-row.title: T-Bar Row
t-bar-row.about: A landmine-style row with a fixed arc that is stable, heavy and great for back thickness.
steps: Straddle the bar and grab the handle or V-grip.
Hinge forward with a flat back and soft knees.
Row the weight toward your upper stomach.
Lower until your arms and back are fully stretched.
cues: Keep the chest up and spine neutral.
Squeeze shoulder blades at the top.
Let the plates almost touch at the bottom for range.

mistakes.text: Standing up and using the hips to swing the weight.
mistakes.fix: Hold a flat-back hinge and row with your arms and back only.

mistakes.text: Loading so heavy that range of motion shrinks.
mistakes.fix: Use a load that lets the plates almost touch at the bottom.

meadows-row.title: Meadows Row
meadows-row.about: A one-arm landmine row with a staggered stance that gives a big stretch and heavy overload.
steps: Stand perpendicular to the end of a landmine bar.
Stagger your stance and rest your free forearm on your knee.
Grip the bar sleeve and let your shoulder stretch down.
Row your elbow up and back past your torso.
Lower slowly into the stretch.
cues: Keep hips square and spine neutral.
Drive the elbow, not the hand.
Use straps if grip limits you.

mistakes.text: Twisting the torso to lift the weight.
mistakes.fix: Keep hips square and spine neutral as you row.

mistakes.text: Jerking the bar up from the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Start each rep from the stretch and drive the elbow smoothly.

seated-cable-row.title: Seated Cable Row
seated-cable-row.about: A stable cable row with constant tension that is easy to overload and offers a big forward stretch.
steps: Sit with feet on the platform and knees softly bent.
Grab the handle and lean forward slightly to stretch the back.
Row to your stomach while bringing the torso upright.
Return slowly, letting shoulders reach forward.
cues: Keep the torso movement small and controlled.
Pull elbows past your ribs and squeeze.
Feel the lats stretch on every return.

mistakes.text: Rocking far back and using body momentum.
mistakes.fix: Keep the torso movement small and pull with your elbows.

mistakes.text: Rounding the lower back under load.
mistakes.fix: Keep a neutral back and lean forward only slightly.

seated-cable-high-elbow-row.title: Seated Cable High-Elbow Row
seated-cable-high-elbow-row.about: A cable row pulled toward the chest with flared elbows to emphasize upper back and rear delts.
steps: Sit at the cable row with a wide or neutral bar.
Reach forward and let the shoulder blades spread.
Row to your lower chest with elbows flared out.
Return slowly until the upper back fully stretches.
cues: Keep elbows roughly 60–90 degrees from the torso.
Pull shoulder blades back, not up.
Stay tall; minimal leaning.

mistakes.text: Shrugging the traps into the pull.
mistakes.fix: Pull your shoulder blades back, not up.

mistakes.text: Turning it into a lean-back swing.
mistakes.fix: Stay tall with minimal leaning and row with your arms and back.

single-arm-cable-row.title: Single-Arm Cable Row
single-arm-cable-row.about: A one-arm cable row with constant tension and a long reach for a strong lat stretch.
steps: Set a single handle at the needed height and sit or kneel.
Reach forward and let the shoulder rotate slightly into the stretch.
Row the handle toward your hip, elbow close.
Return slowly to a long reach.
cues: Keep the torso mostly square to the cable.
Pull to the hip for lats, higher for upper back.
Control the stretch on every rep.

mistakes.text: Twisting the whole body to move the load.
mistakes.fix: Keep the torso mostly square to the cable and move only the arm.

mistakes.text: Letting the cable snap the arm forward.
mistakes.fix: Return slowly to a long reach and control the stretch.

machine-row.title: Machine Row
machine-row.about: A plate-loaded or selectorized row with chest support for stable, heavy back training.
steps: Adjust the seat so handles line up with your mid-chest.
Press your chest into the pad and reach forward.
Row the handles back, driving elbows behind you.
Return slowly to a full forward stretch.
cues: Keep the chest on the pad throughout.
Tuck elbows for lats, flare them for upper back.
Pause for a beat at peak contraction.

mistakes.text: Leaning off the pad to cheat reps.
mistakes.fix: Keep your chest on the pad for the whole set.

mistakes.text: Stopping short of the stretch.
mistakes.fix: Return slowly to a full forward stretch each rep.

thoracic-flexion-extension.title: Thoracic Flexion & Extension
thoracic-flexion-extension.about: A controlled mid-back mobility and strength drill that trains the spinal erectors through flexion and extension.
steps: Sit or kneel tall with hands across your chest or holding light load.
Slowly round your upper back, tucking the chin.
Reverse by extending the mid-back and lifting the chest.
Move segment by segment without using the hips.
cues: Keep the movement in the upper back, not the lower back.
Breathe out as you round, in as you extend.
Use light load and smooth tempo.

mistakes.text: Hinging at the hips instead of moving the spine.
mistakes.fix: Keep your hips still and move segment by segment through the spine.

mistakes.text: Rushing reps or loading too heavy.
mistakes.fix: Use light load and a smooth, slow tempo.

machine-lateral-raise.title: Machine Lateral Raise
machine-lateral-raise.about: A stable lateral raise that lets you push the side delts close to failure safely.
steps: Adjust the seat so your shoulders line up with the machine's pivot.
Place your arms against the pads with a slight elbow bend.
Raise the pads out to the sides until your arms reach shoulder height.
Lower slowly to a full stretch without letting the plates touch.
cues: Push through the elbows, not the hands.
Keep your chest against the pad and shoulders down.
Control the negative for 2–3 seconds.

mistakes.text: Setting the seat so the shoulder sits far from the pivot.
mistakes.fix: Set the seat so your shoulders line up with the machine's pivot.

mistakes.text: Shrugging the shoulders up at the top.
mistakes.fix: Keep shoulders down and push through the elbows.

deadlift.title: Deadlift
deadlift.about: A full posterior-chain hinge that builds total-body strength in the glutes, hamstrings and back.
steps: Stand with mid-foot under the bar, feet hip-width.
Hinge and grip just outside your legs.
Brace, pull slack out of the bar and keep a flat back.
Push the floor away and stand tall with hips through.
Lower the bar along your legs under control.
cues: Keep the bar touching your legs the whole way.
Lock lats by pulling the bar into your body.
Hips and shoulders rise together.

mistakes.text: Rounding the lower back off the floor.
mistakes.fix: Brace and keep a flat back before the bar leaves the floor.

mistakes.text: Jerking the bar instead of building tension first.
mistakes.fix: Pull the slack out of the bar first, then push the floor away.

sumo-deadlift.title: Sumo Deadlift
sumo-deadlift.about: A wide-stance deadlift that trains glutes, adductors and quads with an upright torso.
steps: Stand wide with toes out and the bar over mid-foot.
Grip the bar inside your knees, arms straight.
Push knees out, chest up, and pull slack from the bar.
Push the floor away and lock out with your glutes.
cues: Spread the floor with your feet.
Keep the bar dragging close to your legs.

mistakes.text: Hips shooting up first and rounding the back.
mistakes.fix: Push knees out and keep your chest up as you push the floor away.

mistakes.text: Jerking the bar off the floor.
mistakes.fix: Pull the slack out of the bar before it leaves the floor.

back-extension.title: Back Extension
back-extension.about: A 45° or horizontal hyperextension that strengthens the spinal erectors, glutes and hamstrings safely.
steps: Set the pad just below your hip bones and hook your feet.
Cross arms or hold a plate at your chest.
Hinge down at the hips until you feel a hamstring stretch.
Rise until your body forms a straight line, then lower slowly.
cues: Hinge at the hips with a neutral spine.
Squeeze glutes at the top; don't overarch.
Lower slowly to a deep stretch.

mistakes.text: Hyperextending the lower back at the top.
mistakes.fix: Stop when your body forms a straight line and squeeze glutes.

mistakes.text: Bouncing out of the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly to a deep stretch and rise without bouncing.

spinal-flexion-extension-hyper.title: Hyperextension (Flexion + Extension)
spinal-flexion-extension-hyper.about: A back extension where you round and re-extend the spine to directly train the spinal erectors.
steps: Set up on the hyper bench with the pad at your hips.
Lower down by rounding your back one vertebra at a time.
Pause briefly in the fully rounded stretch.
Uncurl the spine back to neutral, finishing with hips.
cues: Start light; this deliberately loads spinal flexion.
Move slowly and smoothly through each segment.
Stop at a straight line, not an arch.

mistakes.text: Using heavy weight before building tolerance.
mistakes.fix: Start light and add load gradually as tolerance builds.

mistakes.text: Swinging fast through the range.
mistakes.fix: Move slowly and smoothly through each segment.

reverse-hyper.title: Reverse Hyperextension
reverse-hyper.about: A hip-extension movement where the legs move and the torso stays fixed, sparing the spine.
steps: Lie face-down on a reverse hyper or high bench, hips at the edge.
Grip the bench and let your legs hang down.
Squeeze glutes to lift legs up to hip height.
Lower slowly to a full hang.
cues: Drive the movement with glutes, not momentum.
Stop at a straight line; avoid overarching.
Keep the upper body pinned.

mistakes.text: Swinging the legs fast and high.
mistakes.fix: Lift with your glutes under control, only up to hip height.

mistakes.text: Cranking the lower back into hyperextension.
mistakes.fix: Stop at a straight line instead of arching the lower back.

good-morning.title: Good Morning
good-morning.about: A barbell-on-back hinge that loads the hamstrings and glutes in a long stretch.
steps: Rest the bar on your upper back as for a squat.
Unlock the knees slightly and brace.
Push hips back and lower the torso toward parallel.
Drive the hips forward to stand tall.
cues: Keep the spine neutral and the bar over mid-foot.
Start light; the long lever makes it hard.

mistakes.text: Rounding the back at the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Keep the spine neutral and stop when the torso nears parallel.

mistakes.text: Bending the knees so it turns into a squat.
mistakes.fix: Unlock the knees only slightly and push the hips back.

jefferson-curl.title: Jefferson Curl
jefferson-curl.about: A slow, loaded spinal-flexion drill that builds posterior-chain flexibility and spinal resilience.
steps: Stand on a box holding a light weight with straight legs.
Tuck the chin and roll down one vertebra at a time.
Let the weight reach below the box into a deep stretch.
Roll back up slowly, stacking the spine from the bottom.
cues: Use very light load and progress gradually.
Move slowly; two to four seconds each way.
Keep knees straight but not hyperextended.

mistakes.text: Starting too heavy or moving fast.
mistakes.fix: Use a very light load and move two to four seconds each way.

mistakes.text: Hinging at the hips instead of segmentally rolling.
mistakes.fix: Tuck the chin and roll down one vertebra at a time.

hanging-leg-raise.title: Hanging Leg Raise
hanging-leg-raise.about: A straight-leg raise that strongly loads the abs through a long lever, among the hardest ab moves.
steps: Hang from a bar, straps or dip station with a firm brace.
Keep legs straight and together.
Raise your legs as high as possible, curling the pelvis up.
Lower under control without swinging.
cues: Posteriorly tilt the pelvis at the top to involve the abs.
Pause briefly before each rep to stop swinging.

mistakes.text: Using the hip flexors alone with an arched lower back.
mistakes.fix: Tilt the pelvis back at the top to involve the abs.

mistakes.text: Dropping the legs fast between reps.
mistakes.fix: Lower under control and pause briefly before each rep.

barbell-curl.title: Barbell / EZ-Bar Curl
barbell-curl.about: A two-handed curl that lets you load the biceps heavy and progress steadily.
steps: Stand tall holding the bar with an underhand grip.
Pin your elbows at your sides with arms fully straight.
Curl the bar up until forearms are near vertical.
Lower slowly to a full elbow extension.
cues: Keep elbows mostly still; slight forward drift is fine.
Fully straighten the arms at the bottom.
Take two to three seconds on the way down.

mistakes.text: Swinging the torso to heave the bar.
mistakes.fix: Stand tall with elbows pinned at your sides and curl with the arms.

mistakes.text: Half reps that never reach full extension.
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly until your arms are fully straight every rep.

drag-curl.title: Drag Curl
drag-curl.about: A curl where elbows travel back and the weight drags up the torso, keeping biceps tension.
steps: Hold the weight at your thighs with arms straight.
Pull your elbows back as you curl.
Drag the bar or dumbbells up along your torso to the lower chest.
Lower along the same path to full extension.
cues: Keep the weight in contact with, or very close to, your body.
Elbows move behind you, never forward.
Squeeze hard at the top.

mistakes.text: Letting the elbows swing forward into a normal curl.
mistakes.fix: Pull your elbows back and keep the weight close to your body.

mistakes.text: Leaning back to cheat the weight up.
mistakes.fix: Stand still and use a weight you can drag up without leaning.

reverse-curl.title: Reverse Grip Curl
reverse-curl.about: An overhand curl that emphasizes the brachioradialis and forearm extensors.
steps: Grip the bar overhand at about shoulder width, arms straight.
Pin your elbows to your sides.
Curl the bar up until the forearms are near vertical.
Lower slowly until the arms are fully straight.
cues: Keep the wrists neutral, not bent back.
Elbows stay still; no swinging.
Control the full lowering phase.

mistakes.text: Letting the wrists collapse under the bar.
mistakes.fix: Keep the wrists neutral, not bent back.

mistakes.text: Using the hips to swing the bar up.
mistakes.fix: Pin your elbows to your sides and keep the hips still.

finger-flexor-curl.title: Finger Curl
finger-flexor-curl.about: Isolates the finger flexors to build crushing grip strength and forearm size.
steps: Hold the handles or weight with palms up and wrists supported.
Open the fingers and let the weight roll down to the fingertips.
Close the fingers into a tight fist, curling the weight back up.
Open the hand slowly and repeat.
cues: Keep the wrist still; only the fingers move.
Squeeze hard at the top.
Use a full open-to-closed range.

mistakes.text: Turning it into a wrist curl.
mistakes.fix: Keep the wrist still; only the fingers move.

mistakes.text: Using a load so heavy the weight slips from the fingers.
mistakes.fix: Use a load you can roll to the fingertips and back.

preacher-curl.title: Preacher Curl
preacher-curl.about: A pad-supported curl that removes cheating and loads the biceps hard in the stretched position.
steps: Sit at the preacher bench with armpits snug on the pad.
Grip the weight with arms almost fully straight.
Curl up until just before forearms reach vertical.
Lower slowly into a full stretch.
cues: Keep the back of your arms flat on the pad.
Control the bottom; that is where growth happens.
Don't rest at the top.

mistakes.text: Bouncing out of the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly and control the bottom stretch.

mistakes.text: Lifting the elbows off the pad.
mistakes.fix: Keep the back of your arms flat on the pad.

spider-curl.title: Spider Curl
spider-curl.about: A chest-supported curl with arms hanging vertically, giving peak tension near the top of the rep.
steps: Lie chest-down on an incline bench with arms hanging straight.
Grip the weight with palms forward.
Curl up while keeping upper arms vertical.
Squeeze, then lower slowly to full extension.
cues: Keep upper arms perpendicular to the floor.
Squeeze hard at the top for a second.
Fully straighten arms between reps.

mistakes.text: Swinging the elbows forward to make it easier.
mistakes.fix: Keep upper arms vertical, perpendicular to the floor.

mistakes.text: Lifting the chest off the bench.
mistakes.fix: Keep your chest on the bench for every rep.

incline-dumbbell-curl.title: Incline Dumbbell Curl
incline-dumbbell-curl.about: A curl with arms behind the body that stretches the long head of the biceps under load.
steps: Sit back on an incline bench set around 45–60 degrees.
Let the dumbbells hang straight down behind your torso.
Curl up without letting the elbows drift forward.
Lower slowly until arms are fully straight.
cues: Keep your head and shoulders back on the bench.
Feel the stretch at the bottom of every rep.
Supinate the palms as you curl.

mistakes.text: Bringing elbows forward to shorten the range.
mistakes.fix: Keep elbows still so the dumbbells hang behind your torso.

mistakes.text: Shoulders rolling off the bench.
mistakes.fix: Keep your head and shoulders back on the bench.

dumbbell-curl.title: Dumbbell Curl
dumbbell-curl.about: A free dumbbell curl that lets the wrist supinate fully for complete biceps contraction.
steps: Stand or sit holding dumbbells at your sides.
Start with arms fully straight, palms forward or neutral.
Curl up, turning palms up as you lift.
Lower slowly to full extension.
cues: Keep elbows close and mostly still.
Twist the pinky up at the top for a full squeeze.
Control the eccentric for two to three seconds.

mistakes.text: Swinging the dumbbells with the hips.
mistakes.fix: Keep elbows close and still and curl with the arms only.

mistakes.text: Stopping short of full extension.
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly until your arms are fully straight.

hammer-curl.title: Hammer Curl
hammer-curl.about: A neutral-grip curl that targets the brachialis and brachioradialis for thicker upper arms and forearms.
steps: Hold dumbbells at your sides with palms facing each other.
Keep elbows tucked and arms straight.
Curl up without rotating the wrists.
Lower slowly to full extension.
cues: Thumbs stay pointing up the whole rep.
Keep upper arms still.
Lower under control.

mistakes.text: Swinging the torso to move heavy weight.
mistakes.fix: Keep the torso and upper arms still and curl with the forearms.

mistakes.text: Letting elbows flare out to the sides.
mistakes.fix: Keep elbows tucked close to your sides.

concentration-curl.title: Concentration Curl
concentration-curl.about: A seated one-arm curl braced against the thigh that isolates the biceps with zero momentum.
steps: Sit on a bench and brace the back of your upper arm on your inner thigh.
Let the dumbbell hang with your arm fully straight.
Curl up toward your shoulder, rotating the palm up.
Lower slowly to full extension.
cues: Keep the upper arm fixed against the thigh.
Squeeze hard at the top.
Finish every rep with a straight arm.

mistakes.text: Using the thigh or torso to bump the weight up.
mistakes.fix: Keep the upper arm fixed against the thigh and curl with the arm.

mistakes.text: Short reps that skip the stretch.
mistakes.fix: Finish every rep with a straight arm.

cable-curl.title: Cable Curl
cable-curl.about: A standing cable curl that keeps tension on the biceps through the entire range.
steps: Attach a bar or handle to a low pulley and stand facing it.
Grip underhand with arms fully straight.
Curl up while keeping elbows near your sides.
Lower slowly until arms are straight again.
cues: Step back slightly so tension stays on at the bottom.
Keep the torso still.
Control every eccentric.

mistakes.text: Leaning back and using body weight.
mistakes.fix: Keep the torso still and curl with the arms only.

mistakes.text: Elbows sliding far forward at the top.
mistakes.fix: Keep elbows near your sides at the top.

behind-body-cable-curl.title: Behind-the-Body Cable Curl
behind-body-cable-curl.about: A cable curl with the arm behind the torso that stretches the biceps long head under constant tension.
steps: Set the pulley low and face away from the stack.
Step forward so the arm is pulled behind your body.
Curl up while keeping the upper arm back.
Lower slowly into a deep biceps stretch.
cues: Keep the elbow behind the torso throughout.
Use a staggered stance for stability.
Pause briefly in the stretch.

mistakes.text: Letting the elbow swing forward.
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbow behind your torso throughout.

mistakes.text: Going too heavy and losing the stretch.
mistakes.fix: Use a weight that lets you lower into a deep stretch.

lying-cable-curl.title: Lying Cable Curl
lying-cable-curl.about: A curl lying on your back at a low pulley that removes body English for strict biceps work.
steps: Lie on your back with feet toward a low pulley.
Hold the bar with arms straight along your body.
Curl the bar toward your forehead or chest.
Lower slowly to full extension.
cues: Keep upper arms pinned to the floor or bench.
Squeeze at the top for a beat.
Straighten fully between reps.

mistakes.text: Lifting the elbows off the floor.
mistakes.fix: Keep upper arms pinned to the floor or bench.

mistakes.text: Rushing the eccentric.
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly to full extension.

machine-curl.title: Machine Biceps Curl
machine-curl.about: A guided curl machine that provides stable resistance so you can push the biceps close to failure.
steps: Adjust the seat so elbows line up with the machine's pivot.
Rest upper arms on the pad and grip the handles.
Curl up until fully contracted.
Lower slowly to a full stretch.
cues: Keep elbows aligned with the pivot point.
Don't lift your hips or lean back.
Use full range; the machine makes it safe.

mistakes.text: Wrong seat height that misaligns the elbows.
mistakes.fix: Set the seat so your elbows line up with the machine's pivot.

mistakes.text: Stopping before full extension.
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly to a full stretch every rep.

bodyweight-curl.title: Bodyweight Curl
bodyweight-curl.about: A suspended or bar curl using your own body weight to train biceps without equipment.
steps: Grab a low bar or rings underhand and lean back with straight arms.
Keep your body rigid from heels to head.
Curl your body up by bending only at the elbows.
Lower slowly to straight arms.
cues: Keep elbows pointing forward; don't row.
Walk feet forward to make it harder.
Squeeze glutes to avoid sagging.

mistakes.text: Turning it into a row by pulling elbows back.
mistakes.fix: Keep elbows pointing forward and bend only at the elbows.

mistakes.text: Letting the hips drop.
mistakes.fix: Squeeze glutes to keep your body rigid from heels to head.

neutral-dumbbell-press.title: Neutral-Grip Dumbbell Shoulder Press
neutral-dumbbell-press.about: A seated overhead press with palms facing each other that is joint-friendly for the shoulders.
steps: Sit on an upright bench with dumbbells at shoulder height, palms facing in.
Brace your core and keep your back on the pad.
Press the dumbbells overhead until arms are nearly straight.
Lower slowly until the dumbbells reach shoulder level.
cues: Keep elbows slightly in front of your body.
Lower to a deep but comfortable bottom position.
Don't arch the lower back to finish reps.

mistakes.text: Cutting the bottom of the rep short.
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly until the dumbbells reach shoulder level.

mistakes.text: Leaning back into an incline press.
mistakes.fix: Brace your core and keep your back on the pad.

barbell-incline-press.title: Incline Barbell Press
barbell-incline-press.about: A heavy compound press on an incline bench that biases the upper (clavicular) chest.
steps: Set the bench to about 15–30 degrees and lie with eyes under the bar.
Grip slightly wider than shoulders and pull your shoulder blades back and down.
Lower the bar under control to your upper chest.
Press up and slightly back until your arms are straight.
cues: Keep elbows about 45–60 degrees from your torso.
Touch the chest lightly every rep for full range.
Take 2–3 seconds on the way down.

mistakes.text: Bouncing the bar off the chest.
mistakes.fix: Lower for 2–3 seconds and touch the chest lightly.

mistakes.text: Setting the bench so steep that shoulders take over.
mistakes.fix: Set the bench to about 15–30 degrees.

barrel-press.title: Barrel Press
barrel-press.about: A dumbbell press with a wide, hugging arc that stretches the pecs and adds adduction at the top.
steps: Lie on the bench with dumbbells held wide at chest level, elbows flared.
Lower the weights out and down until you feel a deep chest stretch.
Press up in an arc, as if hugging a large barrel.
Bring the dumbbells close together over your chest and squeeze.
cues: Think of pulling your upper arms across your body, not just pushing up.
Keep a slight bend at the top so tension stays on the chest.

mistakes.text: Turning it into a straight-up press with no arc.
mistakes.fix: Press up in an arc, pulling your upper arms across your body.

mistakes.text: Cutting the bottom short and losing the stretch.
mistakes.fix: Lower out and down until you feel a deep chest stretch.

decline-press.title: Decline Press
decline-press.about: A press on a slight decline that emphasizes the lower (sternal) chest with less shoulder stress.
steps: Set a slight decline and lock your legs or feet in place.
Retract your shoulder blades and unrack the weight over your lower chest.
Lower slowly to the lower chest with elbows about 45 degrees.
Press back up to straight arms.
cues: Keep the shoulder blades pinned throughout.
Control the descent; feel the lower pecs stretch.

mistakes.text: Using a steep decline that shortens the range.
mistakes.fix: Use only a slight decline so you keep full range.

mistakes.text: Letting the dumbbells or bar drift toward the neck.
mistakes.fix: Lower to the lower chest with elbows about 45 degrees.

reverse-grip-press.title: Reverse Grip Press
reverse-grip-press.about: An underhand bench press that keeps elbows tucked, biasing the upper chest and triceps.
steps: Grip the bar palms facing you, slightly wider than shoulder width.
Retract your shoulder blades and unrack with a spotter or Smith machine.
Lower the bar to your lower chest with elbows tucked close.
Press up and slightly back toward your face.
cues: Wrap the thumbs fully around the bar for safety.
Start light; the bar path feels different from a normal press.

mistakes.text: Using a thumbless grip with an underhand bar.
mistakes.fix: Wrap your thumbs fully around the bar.

mistakes.text: Flaring elbows wide, which strains the wrists.
mistakes.fix: Keep elbows tucked close as you lower to the lower chest.

floor-press.title: Floor Press
floor-press.about: A press from the floor that limits depth, building lockout strength while sparing the shoulders.
steps: Lie on the floor with knees bent and weights over your chest.
Lower until your upper arms gently touch the floor.
Pause briefly without relaxing.
Press back up to straight arms.
cues: Keep elbows around 45 degrees from your body.
Let arms touch the floor softly, never slam.

mistakes.text: Bouncing elbows off the floor.
mistakes.fix: Touch the floor softly with your upper arms and pause briefly.

mistakes.text: Letting the wrists bend far back.
mistakes.fix: Keep your wrists straight over your elbows.

flat-dumbbell-press.title: Flat Dumbbell Press
flat-dumbbell-press.about: A flat-bench press with dumbbells that allows a deeper stretch than a barbell.
steps: Sit with dumbbells on your thighs, then kick them up as you lie back.
Retract your shoulder blades and plant your feet.
Lower the dumbbells beside your chest until you feel a full stretch.
Press up and slightly in until arms are nearly straight.
cues: Elbows about 45–60 degrees, forearms vertical.
Spend 2–3 seconds lowering; drive up with intent.

mistakes.text: Stopping short of a full stretch at the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Lower the dumbbells beside your chest until you feel a full stretch.

mistakes.text: Clanging dumbbells together and losing tension.
mistakes.fix: Press up and slightly in, stopping before the dumbbells touch.

incline-dumbbell-press.title: Incline Dumbbell Press
incline-dumbbell-press.about: An incline dumbbell press that targets the upper chest through a long, deep range of motion.
steps: Set the bench to about 15–45 degrees and kick the dumbbells up.
Pin your shoulder blades back and down against the bench.
Lower the dumbbells to upper-chest level until you feel a deep stretch.
Press up and slightly together over your upper chest.
cues: A lower incline (15–30°) keeps more work on the chest.
Keep forearms stacked under the dumbbells.
Control the eccentric for 2–3 seconds.

mistakes.text: Shrugging the shoulders up off the bench.
mistakes.fix: Pin your shoulder blades back and down against the bench.

mistakes.text: Half reps that skip the stretched position.
mistakes.fix: Lower to upper-chest level until you feel a deep stretch.

supinated-dumbbell-press.title: Slightly Supinated Dumbbell Press
supinated-dumbbell-press.about: A dumbbell press with palms turned slightly toward you, tucking elbows to bias the upper chest.
steps: Sit on a bench set to a slight or moderate incline.
Hold the dumbbells with pinkies turned slightly inward toward each other.
Lower with elbows tucked about 30–45 degrees to a deep stretch.
Press up toward your upper chest line, keeping the grip angle.
cues: Keep the slight supinated angle the whole set.
Drive the upper arm up and in toward your face.

mistakes.text: Flaring elbows and losing the tucked path.
mistakes.fix: Keep elbows tucked about 30–45 degrees the whole set.

mistakes.text: Rushing the descent and bouncing out of the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly into the deep stretch and press up smoothly.

seated-barbell-press.title: Seated Barbell Press
seated-barbell-press.about: A seated overhead press that builds the front delts with upper-chest and triceps assistance.
steps: Sit upright on a bench with back support and grip just outside shoulders.
Start with the bar at upper-chest or chin level.
Press straight overhead, moving your head back slightly to clear the bar.
Lower under control to the start.
cues: Brace your abs and avoid arching your lower back.
Keep forearms vertical under the bar.

mistakes.text: Leaning far back and turning it into an incline press.
mistakes.fix: Sit upright, brace your abs and press straight overhead.

mistakes.text: Cutting the bottom short of chin level.
mistakes.fix: Lower under control to chin or upper-chest level each rep.

raise-to-press.title: Raise To Press
raise-to-press.about: A combo of a front raise into a press that hammers the front delts and upper chest.
steps: Sit upright holding dumbbells at your thighs, palms facing in.
Raise the dumbbells in front to shoulder height, touching them together.
Bend the elbows and bring them to your shoulders.
Press overhead, then reverse the sequence slowly.
cues: Keep the torso still; no swinging.
Use light weights and smooth transitions.

mistakes.text: Using momentum to lift the dumbbells.
mistakes.fix: Keep the torso still and use light weights.

mistakes.text: Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears.
mistakes.fix: Keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.

smith-incline-press.title: Smith Incline Press
smith-incline-press.about: A Smith machine incline press; the fixed path lets you push hard and safely for the upper chest.
steps: Set the bench at 15–45 degrees so the bar lands on your upper chest.
Grip slightly wider than shoulders and retract your shoulder blades.
Unrack and lower slowly until the bar touches your upper chest.
Press up to near lockout.
cues: Check bench position first so the bar path matches your chest.
Keep elbows 45–60 degrees; tuck more for upper chest focus.

mistakes.text: Bench too far forward or back, so the bar hits your neck or belly.
mistakes.fix: Check bench position first so the bar lands on your upper chest.

mistakes.text: Bouncing the bar off the chest.
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly until the bar touches your upper chest.

machine-chest-press.title: Machine Chest Press
machine-chest-press.about: A stable machine press that lets you train the chest close to failure with low skill demand.
steps: Adjust the seat so the handles line up with mid-to-lower chest.
Sit tall, chest up, shoulder blades pulled back into the pad.
Press the handles forward until your arms are nearly straight.
Return slowly until you feel a strong chest stretch.
cues: Keep your back and head on the pad.
Let the handles come back far for a full stretch.
Lower in 2–3 seconds every rep.

mistakes.text: Seat too low or high, shifting work to the shoulders.
mistakes.fix: Set the seat so the handles line up with mid-to-lower chest.

mistakes.text: Letting the weight stack slam between reps.
mistakes.fix: Lower in 2–3 seconds into a strong chest stretch.

machine-incline-press.title: Machine Incline Press
machine-incline-press.about: An incline press machine for the upper chest that's easy to push safely to failure.
steps: Set the seat so handles start around upper-chest height.
Sit back with shoulder blades retracted and feet planted.
Press up and forward until arms are nearly straight.
Lower slowly into a deep upper-chest stretch.
cues: Keep elbows slightly below shoulder height.
Pause briefly in the stretch without relaxing.

mistakes.text: Lifting the hips or chest off the pad to grind reps.
mistakes.fix: Sit back with shoulder blades retracted and feet planted.

mistakes.text: Short, fast reps that skip the stretch.
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly and pause briefly in the stretch.

dumbbell-fly.title: Dumbbell Fly
dumbbell-fly.about: A flat-bench fly that loads the chest hard in the stretched position, a strong growth stimulus.
steps: Lie flat holding dumbbells over your chest, palms facing each other.
Keep a soft, fixed bend in the elbows.
Open your arms in a wide arc until you feel a deep chest stretch.
Bring the dumbbells back up along the same arc.
cues: Move only at the shoulders; the elbow angle stays locked.
Spend most effort in the bottom half where tension is highest.

mistakes.text: Bending and straightening the elbows, turning it into a press.
mistakes.fix: Keep a soft, fixed elbow bend and move only at the shoulders.

mistakes.text: Going too heavy and dropping below a safe stretch.
mistakes.fix: Use a weight that lets you stop at a deep but safe stretch.

incline-dumbbell-fly.title: Incline Dumbbell Fly
incline-dumbbell-fly.about: A fly on an incline bench that targets the upper chest in a deep stretch.
steps: Set the bench to about 15–45 degrees and lie back with dumbbells up.
Keep a slight bend in the elbows, palms facing each other.
Lower in a wide arc until the upper chest is fully stretched.
Sweep the dumbbells up and in toward your upper chest.
cues: Think of bringing your biceps toward your chin.
Control the bottom; don't let the weights drop.

mistakes.text: Pressing the weights instead of hugging them up.
mistakes.fix: Sweep the dumbbells up in an arc, biceps toward your chin.

mistakes.text: Using a bench angle so steep the shoulders take over.
mistakes.fix: Set the bench to about 15–45 degrees.

scoop-fly.title: Seated Dumbbell Scoop Fly
scoop-fly.about: A low-to-high fly that scoops the dumbbells up and in to bias the upper chest.
steps: Sit on an upright or high-incline bench, dumbbells at your sides.
Turn palms forward with a slight bend in the elbows.
Sweep the arms forward and up in an arc to eye level.
Lower slowly back to your sides with a chest stretch.
cues: Lead with the inner arm and squeeze the upper chest at the top.
Keep the shoulders down, away from the ears.

mistakes.text: Turning it into a front raise with no inward path.
mistakes.fix: Sweep forward and up in an arc, leading with the inner arm.

mistakes.text: Swinging the torso to lift the weight.
mistakes.fix: Keep the torso still and move only the arms.

cable-fly.title: Cable Fly
cable-fly.about: A cable fly that keeps constant tension on the chest from full stretch to full squeeze.
steps: Set the pulleys at the height you want and grab a handle in each hand.
Stand in a staggered stance or sit with your back supported.
With soft elbows, let the arms open until the chest is stretched.
Bring the handles together in front of you and squeeze.
cues: Pull from the upper arm, not the hands.
Keep the chest up and shoulders back throughout.
Pause in the stretch, then move smoothly.

mistakes.text: Leaning forward too far and pressing with the arms.
mistakes.fix: Keep the chest up and pull from the upper arm, not the hands.

mistakes.text: Letting the cables yank the arms back uncontrolled.
mistakes.fix: Let the arms open slowly and pause in the stretch.

incline-cable-fly.title: Incline Cable Fly
incline-cable-fly.about: A cable fly on an incline bench that loads the upper chest through a deep stretch.
steps: Place an incline bench between low pulleys at about 15–45 degrees.
Lie back holding the handles above your upper chest.
Open the arms in a wide arc until the upper chest stretches.
Bring the handles up and together over your upper chest.
cues: Keep a soft, fixed elbow bend.
Lower in 2–3 seconds and pause in the stretch.

mistakes.text: Bending the elbows more and more as you tire.
mistakes.fix: Keep a soft, fixed elbow bend on every rep.

mistakes.text: Lifting the shoulders off the bench at the top.
mistakes.fix: Keep your shoulders on the bench as the handles meet.

machine-fly.title: Machine Fly
machine-fly.about: A pec-deck fly that safely loads the chest in a big stretch with steady tension.
steps: Set the seat so handles are at mid-chest height.
Sit with back on the pad and grab the handles with soft elbows.
Bring the handles together in front of your chest and squeeze.
Return slowly until you feel a strong chest stretch.
cues: Keep the chest proud and shoulder blades back.
Set the start position for the deepest stretch you can control.

mistakes.text: Rolling the shoulders forward at the squeeze.
mistakes.fix: Keep the chest proud and shoulder blades back as you squeeze.

mistakes.text: Letting the weight stack drop at the stretch.
mistakes.fix: Return slowly into the stretch you can control.

rear-cable-fly-protraction.title: Cable Fly With Protraction
rear-cable-fly-protraction.about: A cable fly from pulleys behind you that finishes with a forward reach to fully shorten the chest.
steps: Set the pulleys around chest height and face away from the machine.
Hold the handles with a slight elbow bend and arms open wide.
Sweep the arms together in front, rotating the upper arms slightly outward.
At the end, reach forward by spreading the shoulder blades, then return slowly.
cues: Let the shoulder blades pull back in the stretch, forward at the finish.
Keep the ribcage down and torso still.

mistakes.text: Shrugging the shoulders up during the reach.
mistakes.fix: Reach forward by spreading the shoulder blades, keeping shoulders down.

mistakes.text: Rushing back so the cables yank the arms open.
mistakes.fix: Return slowly so the arms open under control.

around-the-worlds.title: Around The Worlds
around-the-worlds.about: A light dumbbell arc from hips to overhead that stretches the chest and works shoulder mobility.
steps: Lie flat holding light dumbbells at your thighs, palms up.
Keep elbows slightly bent and arms just off the floor line.
Sweep the dumbbells out and around in a wide half-circle overhead.
Reverse the arc slowly back to your hips.
cues: Use light weight; this is a control and stretch movement.
Keep the arms roughly parallel to the floor.

mistakes.text: Going heavy and straining the shoulders.
mistakes.fix: Use light weight; this is a control and stretch movement.

mistakes.text: Arching the lower back as the arms go overhead.
mistakes.fix: Keep your ribcage down and lower back flat as arms go overhead.

dips-chest.title: Chest Dips
dips-chest.about: A bodyweight press on parallel bars that deeply stretches the lower chest under load.
steps: Support yourself on parallel bars with arms straight.
Lean your torso forward and let elbows flare slightly.
Lower slowly until you feel a deep chest stretch.
Press back up to straight arms.
cues: Keep shoulders down and away from your ears.
Go only as deep as your shoulders tolerate comfortably.
Lower in 2–3 seconds.

mistakes.text: Staying upright, which shifts work to the triceps.
mistakes.fix: Lean your torso forward and let elbows flare slightly.

mistakes.text: Dropping fast and bouncing at the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Lower in 2–3 seconds, only as deep as your shoulders tolerate.

machine-dips.title: Machine Dips
machine-dips.about: A seated or assisted dip machine that trains chest and triceps with adjustable, stable loading.
steps: Adjust the seat so handles start around lower-chest height.
Grip the handles and sit tall with chest up.
Press the handles down until arms are straight.
Let them rise slowly into a deep stretch.
cues: Lean slightly forward for more chest, upright for triceps.
Keep shoulders depressed throughout.

mistakes.text: Shrugging up as the handles rise.
mistakes.fix: Keep shoulders depressed as the handles rise.

mistakes.text: Using only the bottom half of the range.
mistakes.fix: Let the handles rise slowly into a deep stretch each rep.

push-ups.title: Push-Ups
push-ups.about: The classic bodyweight press for chest, front delts and triceps, with core stability built in.
steps: Place hands slightly wider than shoulders, body straight from head to heels.
Brace your abs and squeeze your glutes.
Lower until your chest nearly touches the floor.
Push the floor away back to straight arms.
cues: Elbows about 45 degrees from your body.
Move as one rigid plank.
Use full range; slow the descent.

mistakes.text: Sagging hips or piking the butt up.
mistakes.fix: Brace abs and glutes to move as one rigid plank.

mistakes.text: Half reps that never reach the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Lower until your chest nearly touches the floor.

deficit-push-ups.title: Deficit Push-Ups
deficit-push-ups.about: Push-ups with hands on dumbbells so the chest drops below hand level for an extra-deep stretch.
steps: Place two dumbbells or handles slightly wider than shoulders.
Grip them and set a straight plank.
Lower slowly past your hands until the chest is deeply stretched.
Pause briefly, then press back up.
cues: Use stable hex dumbbells that won't roll.
Keep the core tight so hips stay level.

mistakes.text: Going deeper than your shoulders can control.
mistakes.fix: Lower only as deep as your shoulders can control.

mistakes.text: Losing the plank as you tire.
mistakes.fix: Keep the core tight so your hips stay level.

chest-stretch.title: Chest Stretch
chest-stretch.about: A static stretch held for about 60 seconds to lengthen the pecs and front shoulders.
steps: Place your forearm on a doorframe or post, elbow at shoulder height.
Step through gently until you feel a stretch across the chest.
Breathe slowly and hold for about 60 seconds.
Switch sides.
cues: Keep the stretch mild to moderate, never painful.
Keep the ribcage down and torso tall.

mistakes.text: Forcing the stretch and straining the shoulder.
mistakes.fix: Keep the stretch mild to moderate, never painful.

mistakes.text: Holding your breath.
mistakes.fix: Breathe slowly throughout the hold.

ball-knee-tuck.title: Exercise Ball Knees To Chest
ball-knee-tuck.about: A plank-based tuck on a stability ball that trains the abs while the chest and shoulders stabilize.
steps: Start in a push-up position with your shins on the ball.
Brace your core and keep arms straight under your shoulders.
Pull your knees toward your chest, rolling the ball forward.
Extend your legs slowly back to the plank.
cues: Round the lower back slightly as the knees come in.
Keep shoulders stacked over your wrists.

mistakes.text: Letting the hips sag at the start position.
mistakes.fix: Brace your core so your body stays straight in the plank.

mistakes.text: Rushing and losing control of the ball.
mistakes.fix: Roll the ball in and extend your legs slowly.

skull-crushers.title: Skull Crushers
skull-crushers.about: A lying barbell or EZ-bar extension that loads all three triceps heads, especially the long head.
steps: Lie on a flat or incline bench holding the bar over your chest.
Tilt your arms slightly back toward your head.
Bend only at the elbows, lowering the bar behind your head.
Extend the elbows to press the bar back up.
cues: Keep the upper arms angled back for long-head stretch.
Elbows stay roughly shoulder-width; don't flare.
Lower in 2–3 seconds.

mistakes.text: Turning it into a press by moving the upper arms.
mistakes.fix: Keep upper arms angled back and bend only at the elbows.

mistakes.text: Stopping short of a deep stretch at the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Lower in 2–3 seconds behind your head into a deep stretch.

dumbbell-skull-crushers.title: Dumbbell Skull Crushers
dumbbell-skull-crushers.about: A lying dumbbell triceps extension; independent arms allow a deep, joint-friendly stretch.
steps: Lie on a bench holding dumbbells over your chest, palms facing in.
Angle the upper arms slightly back toward your head.
Bend the elbows and lower the dumbbells beside your head.
Extend the elbows back to the start.
cues: Keep the upper arms still; only the forearms move.
Reach a full stretch, then lock out under control.

mistakes.text: Letting elbows drift wide apart.
mistakes.fix: Keep the upper arms still with elbows pointing up.

mistakes.text: Dropping the weights fast into the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Lower the dumbbells slowly beside your head.

dead-skulls.title: Dead Skulls
dead-skulls.about: A skull crusher where the weight rests behind your head each rep, removing momentum.
steps: Lie on a bench with the bar or dumbbells resting on the bench behind your head.
Grip the weight with upper arms angled back.
Extend the elbows to lift the weight from a dead stop to straight arms.
Lower slowly and let the weight settle fully before the next rep.
cues: Start each rep with no bounce or stretch reflex.
Keep elbows narrow and pointing up.

mistakes.text: Bouncing the weight off the bench.
mistakes.fix: Let the weight settle fully and start each rep from a dead stop.

mistakes.text: Pulling with the lats instead of extending the elbows.
mistakes.fix: Keep upper arms angled back and extend only at the elbows.

french-press.title: French Press
french-press.about: An overhead triceps extension that trains the long head in its most stretched position.
steps: Sit or stand tall holding the bar or dumbbell overhead.
Keep the upper arms close to your head, elbows pointing forward.
Lower the weight behind your head until the triceps fully stretch.
Extend the elbows to press it back overhead.
cues: Brace your abs to keep the lower back neutral.
Prioritize the deep stretch at the bottom.
Control a 2–3 second eccentric.

mistakes.text: Flaring the elbows wide.
mistakes.fix: Keep upper arms close to your head with elbows pointing forward.

mistakes.text: Arching the lower back to push the weight.
mistakes.fix: Brace your abs to keep the lower back neutral.

single-arm-overhead-extension.title: Single Arm Overhead Extension
single-arm-overhead-extension.about: A one-arm overhead extension that stretches the long head and fixes left-right imbalances.
steps: Hold a dumbbell overhead in one hand, upper arm by your ear.
Support your elbow or brace with the free hand if needed.
Lower the weight behind your head into a deep stretch.
Extend the elbow fully, then repeat and switch arms.
cues: Keep the upper arm vertical and still.
Squeeze the triceps at the top without slamming.

mistakes.text: Letting the elbow drift out to the side.
mistakes.fix: Keep the upper arm vertical, right by your ear.

mistakes.text: Leaning the torso to help the rep.
mistakes.fix: Keep the torso still and support the elbow with your free hand.

cable-overhead-extension.title: Cable Overhead Extension
cable-overhead-extension.about: An overhead cable extension that keeps tension on the long head through a deep stretch.
steps: Attach a rope or bar to a low or mid pulley and face away.
Bring the handle behind your head with elbows pointing forward.
Step forward into a split stance and lean slightly.
Extend the elbows forward and up, then return slowly to a full stretch.
cues: Keep the upper arms fixed beside your head.
Let the cable pull you into a deep stretch each rep.

mistakes.text: Moving the shoulders and turning it into a pullover.
mistakes.fix: Keep the upper arms fixed beside your head; move only the elbows.

mistakes.text: Cutting the stretch short at the back.
mistakes.fix: Return slowly and let the cable pull you into a full stretch.

incline-cable-extension.title: Incline Cable Extension
incline-cable-extension.about: A cable skull crusher on an incline bench; the cable keeps the long head loaded at full stretch.
steps: Place an incline bench in front of a low pulley, head toward the cable.
Lie back holding the attachment with arms pointing up and slightly back.
Bend the elbows and let the cable pull your hands behind your head.
Extend the elbows until arms are straight.
cues: Hold the upper arm angle fixed; only the elbows move.
Pause in the stretch for a moment.

mistakes.text: Letting the elbows drift forward as you extend.
mistakes.fix: Hold the upper arm angle fixed; only the elbows move.

mistakes.text: Using a weight so heavy you shorten the stretch.
mistakes.fix: Use a weight that lets you pause in the full stretch.

bar-pushdown.title: Straight Bar Pushdown
bar-pushdown.about: A cable pushdown with a straight, EZ or V-bar that targets the lateral and medial triceps heads.
steps: Attach a bar to a high pulley and grip it about shoulder width.
Pin your elbows to your sides with a slight forward lean.
Push the bar down until your arms are fully straight.
Let it rise slowly until forearms pass parallel to the floor.
cues: Keep the elbows still; only the forearms move.
Fully lock out and squeeze at the bottom.

mistakes.text: Leaning over the bar and pushing with bodyweight.
mistakes.fix: Keep a slight lean and push with the triceps, not your bodyweight.

mistakes.text: Letting elbows flare or drift forward.
mistakes.fix: Pin your elbows to your sides; only the forearms move.

rope-pushdown.title: Rope Pushdown
rope-pushdown.about: A rope cable pushdown; spreading the rope at the bottom gives a strong lateral-head squeeze.
steps: Attach a rope to a high pulley and grip the ends, thumbs up.
Tuck the elbows by your sides and stand tall.
Push down and spread the rope apart at the bottom.
Return slowly until the forearms rise past parallel.
cues: Lock out fully and pull the rope ends outward.
Keep the upper arms pinned throughout.

mistakes.text: Swinging the torso to move the weight.
mistakes.fix: Stand tall and keep the upper arms pinned.

mistakes.text: Short reps that never reach lockout.
mistakes.fix: Lock out fully and pull the rope ends outward at the bottom.

single-arm-pushdown.title: Single Arm Cable Pushdown
single-arm-pushdown.about: A one-arm cable pushdown that lets you groove the elbow path and balance both sides.
steps: Grab a single handle on a high pulley with one hand.
Pin the elbow to your side and brace with the free hand.
Extend the elbow until the arm is fully straight.
Return slowly until the forearm is above parallel.
cues: Keep the shoulder down and torso square.
Squeeze hard at full lockout.

mistakes.text: Rotating the torso to help the arm.
mistakes.fix: Keep the torso square and brace with the free hand.

mistakes.text: Letting the elbow travel forward.
mistakes.fix: Pin the elbow to your side for the whole rep.

incline-cable-pushdown.title: Incline Cable Pushdown
incline-cable-pushdown.about: A pushdown done lying on an incline bench, changing the arm angle to load the triceps differently.
steps: Set an incline bench facing away from a high pulley.
Lie back and grab the attachment above your head with elbows bent.
Keep the upper arms fixed and extend the elbows toward your hips.
Return slowly until the forearms fold back fully.
cues: Lock the upper arms in place; only the elbows bend.
Pause at full extension and squeeze.

mistakes.text: Pulling with the lats so the upper arms move.
mistakes.fix: Lock the upper arms in place; only the elbows bend.

mistakes.text: Rushing the return and losing tension.
mistakes.fix: Return slowly until the forearms fold back fully.

close-grip-press.title: Close Grip Bench Press
close-grip-press.about: A narrow-grip bench press that shifts load to the triceps while still training the chest heavy.
steps: Lie on a flat bench and grip the bar about shoulder width.
Retract the shoulder blades and unrack over your chest.
Lower the bar to your lower chest, elbows close to your sides.
Press up by driving through the triceps to lockout.
cues: Shoulder-width is enough; too narrow strains the wrists.
Keep the wrists stacked over the elbows.
Lower in 2–3 seconds.

mistakes.text: Gripping so narrow the wrists bend painfully.
mistakes.fix: Grip about shoulder width with wrists stacked over elbows.

mistakes.text: Flaring the elbows and losing triceps focus.
mistakes.fix: Keep elbows close to your sides as you lower to the lower chest.

jm-press.title: JM Press
jm-press.about: A hybrid of a close-grip press and skull crusher that overloads the triceps with heavy weight.
steps: Lie on a bench holding the bar or dumbbells over your chest, close grip.
Lower by bending the elbows and letting them drift forward slightly.
Bring the weight toward your chin or upper chest, forearms angled back.
Extend the elbows to press back to lockout.
cues: Elbows stay tucked and point toward your feet.
Lower slowly; the stretch is where it works.

mistakes.text: Turning it into a regular bench press.
mistakes.fix: Keep elbows tucked, pointing toward your feet, forearms angled back.

mistakes.text: Letting the weight crash toward your face.
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly toward your chin or upper chest.

triceps-dips.title: Triceps Dips
triceps-dips.about: An upright dip that loads the triceps heavily with bodyweight or added weight.
steps: Support yourself on parallel bars or a straight bar with arms locked.
Keep the torso upright and elbows pointing back.
Lower until the upper arms are about parallel or slightly below.
Press back up to full lockout.
cues: Stay vertical to keep the work on the triceps.
Keep shoulders down and chest up.

mistakes.text: Leaning far forward, which turns it into a chest dip.
mistakes.fix: Keep the torso upright with elbows pointing back.

mistakes.text: Dropping too deep with the shoulders rolling forward.
mistakes.fix: Lower until upper arms are about parallel, shoulders down.

bench-dips.title: Bench Dips
bench-dips.about: A bodyweight triceps exercise using a bench behind you; easy to scale by moving the feet.
steps: Place your hands on a bench behind you, fingers forward.
Extend your legs in front; bend knees to make it easier.
Lower your hips by bending the elbows to about 90 degrees.
Press through your palms back to straight arms.
cues: Keep your hips close to the bench.
Point the elbows straight back, not out.

mistakes.text: Going so deep the shoulders roll forward painfully.
mistakes.fix: Bend the elbows to about 90 degrees and no deeper.

mistakes.text: Pushing with the legs instead of the arms.
mistakes.fix: Press through your palms and keep the legs passive.

triceps-push-ups.title: Triceps Push-Ups
triceps-push-ups.about: A close-hand push-up with tucked elbows that shifts work from the chest to the triceps.
steps: Set hands shoulder width or slightly narrower, body in a straight plank.
Brace your core and glutes.
Lower with elbows tight to your ribs until the chest nears the floor.
Press back up to full lockout.
cues: Elbows brush your sides and point back.
Squeeze the triceps at the top.

mistakes.text: Flaring the elbows out like a normal push-up.
mistakes.fix: Keep elbows tight to your ribs, pointing back.

mistakes.text: Placing hands so narrow the wrists hurt.
mistakes.fix: Set hands about shoulder width, or only slightly narrower.

kickback.title: Dumbbell Kickback
kickback.about: A dumbbell extension with the upper arm behind the body, peaking tension at full lockout.
steps: Lie chest-down on a slight incline bench, or hinge forward, dumbbells in hand.
Raise the upper arms to your sides, parallel to your torso.
Extend the elbows until the arms are fully straight behind you.
Lower the forearms slowly to vertical.
cues: Keep the upper arms still and high.
Squeeze at lockout for a moment.

mistakes.text: Swinging the weight with the shoulder.
mistakes.fix: Keep the upper arms still and move only the forearms.

mistakes.text: Letting the upper arm drop as you tire.
mistakes.fix: Keep the upper arms high, parallel to your torso.

bodyweight-triceps-extension.title: Bodyweight French Press
bodyweight-triceps-extension.about: A bodyweight skull crusher on a bar or bench that strongly loads the triceps with no equipment.
steps: Grip a bar or bench edge at about hip height, hands shoulder width.
Walk your feet back into a straight, leaning plank.
Bend only the elbows, lowering your head under the bar.
Extend the elbows to push back to straight arms.
cues: Keep the body rigid from head to heels.
Move feet back to make it harder, forward to make it easier.

mistakes.text: Bending at the hips instead of the elbows.
mistakes.fix: Keep the body rigid from head to heels and bend only the elbows.

mistakes.text: Letting the elbows flare wide.
mistakes.fix: Keep elbows about shoulder width as you lower.

hack-squat.title: Hack Squat
hack-squat.about: A machine squat that loads the quads deeply with a stable back, so you can push close to failure safely.
steps: Set your back flat on the pad and shoulders under the pads.
Place feet shoulder-width, low enough on the platform for knees to travel forward.
Release the safeties and lower slowly until your thighs pass parallel.
Drive through the whole foot back to just short of lockout.
cues: Let the knees travel well past the toes for a deep quad stretch.
Control a 2–3 second descent and keep your hips on the pad.

mistakes.text: Cutting depth short to lift more weight.
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly until your thighs pass parallel on every rep.

mistakes.text: Letting the heels or lower back lift off as you bottom out.
mistakes.fix: Keep your back and hips on the pad and drive through the whole foot.

leg-press.title: Leg Press
leg-press.about: A stable, heavily loadable press that builds the quads and glutes with low demand on the lower back.
steps: Sit with your back and hips pressed into the seat.
Place feet hip- to shoulder-width in the middle of the platform.
Unlock the sled and lower until knees are deeply bent without your hips rolling up.
Press through mid-foot and heel to just before lockout.
cues: Go as deep as you can while your tailbone stays on the pad.
Keep knees tracking in line with your toes.

mistakes.text: Bouncing out of the bottom instead of controlling the turnaround.
mistakes.fix: Lower under control and reverse smoothly at the bottom.

mistakes.text: Snapping the knees into hard lockout at the top.
mistakes.fix: Press to just before lockout, keeping the knees soft.

leg-extension.title: Leg Extension
leg-extension.about: The best isolation for the quads, including the rectus femoris, which squats train poorly.
steps: Adjust the seat so your knees line up with the machine's pivot.
Set the pad on your lower shin, just above the ankle.
Hold the handles and extend your knees until the legs are straight.
Squeeze briefly, then lower slowly until the knees are fully bent.
cues: Lean back slightly to stretch the rectus femoris more.
Control the lowering phase for 2–3 seconds.

mistakes.text: Swinging the weight up with momentum.
mistakes.fix: Extend smoothly and lower for 2–3 seconds.

mistakes.text: Stopping short of the deep, bent-knee bottom position.
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly until the knees are fully bent each rep.

high-bar-squat.title: High Bar Squat
high-bar-squat.about: A free-weight squat with an upright torso that builds the quads, glutes and adductors through a long range.
steps: Rest the bar on your upper traps and brace your core.
Stand with feet about shoulder-width, toes slightly out.
Sit straight down between your heels, knees pushing forward and out.
Descend below parallel, then drive up keeping your chest tall.
cues: Take a big breath and brace before each rep.
Keep the bar over mid-foot throughout.

mistakes.text: Letting the knees cave inward on the way up.
mistakes.fix: Push your knees out in line with your toes as you stand.

mistakes.text: Hips shooting up first so the squat turns into a good morning.
mistakes.fix: Drive up keeping your chest tall and the bar over mid-foot.

low-bar-squat.title: Low Bar Squat
low-bar-squat.about: A squat with the bar lower on the back and more forward lean, shifting load toward glutes and adductors.
steps: Place the bar across your rear delts, below the top of the traps.
Grip firmly and pull elbows back to lock the bar in.
Push hips back and down while leaning your torso forward.
Reach at least parallel, then drive hips and chest up together.
cues: Keep the bar over mid-foot as you lean.
Brace hard and keep a neutral spine.

mistakes.text: Rounding the lower back at the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Brace hard and keep a neutral spine to the bottom.

mistakes.text: Letting the bar slide down the back during the rep.
mistakes.fix: Grip firmly and pull your elbows back to lock the bar in.

front-squat.title: Front Squat
front-squat.about: Holding the load in front keeps you very upright, making this a highly quad-focused squat.
steps: Rest the weight on your front delts with elbows high.
Set feet shoulder-width; elevate heels if ankles are stiff.
Sit straight down, letting knees travel far forward.
Go as deep as you can, then stand up keeping elbows high.
cues: Think elbows up to stop the torso folding forward.
Stay tall and brace your core throughout.

mistakes.text: Dropping the elbows so the weight rolls forward.
mistakes.fix: Keep your elbows high throughout the rep.

mistakes.text: Shortening depth instead of using heel elevation.
mistakes.fix: Elevate your heels if ankles are stiff and keep full depth.

smith-squat.title: Smith Squat
smith-squat.about: The fixed bar path lets you place your feet freely and focus on pushing the quads hard with less balance demand.
steps: Set the bar on your upper back and unrack it.
Place feet slightly forward or under the bar to suit your target.
Lower under control until thighs pass parallel.
Drive up through the whole foot without locking out hard.
cues: Feet under the bar bias quads; feet forward bias glutes.
Keep a steady 2–3 second lowering phase.

mistakes.text: Placing feet so far forward that the lower back rounds.
mistakes.fix: Place your feet only as far forward as your back stays neutral.

mistakes.text: Dropping fast and bouncing off the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Lower steadily for 2–3 seconds and drive up smoothly.

belt-squat.title: Belt Squat
belt-squat.about: Loads the legs through a hip belt, training deep squats with no load on the spine.
steps: Attach the belt around your hips and stand on the platform.
Set feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out.
Hold the rails lightly and squat down as deep as is comfortable.
Drive up through mid-foot to standing.
cues: Stay upright and let the knees travel forward.
Use full depth since your back is not limiting you.

mistakes.text: Pulling hard on the handles to assist the lift.
mistakes.fix: Hold the rails lightly and drive up through mid-foot.

mistakes.text: Rushing the descent and losing tension at the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Lower under control and stay tight at the bottom.

sissy-squat.title: Sissy Squat
sissy-squat.about: Knees travel far forward while hips stay extended, giving a huge stretch on all four quad heads.
steps: Hold a support or the load and rise onto the balls of your feet.
Push your knees forward and lean back, keeping hips straight.
Lower until your knees are deeply bent and the quads are fully stretched.
Drive the knees back to return to standing.
cues: Keep a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Lower slowly; the stretched bottom is where the growth is.

mistakes.text: Bending at the hips, which turns it into a normal squat.
mistakes.fix: Keep a straight line from knees to shoulders as you lower.

mistakes.text: Adding load before you own the bodyweight range.
mistakes.fix: Master the full bodyweight range before adding load.

somersault-squat.title: Somersault Squat
somersault-squat.about: A hybrid of sissy and regular squat: knees drive far forward on the toes for a deep quad stretch.
steps: Stand tall holding the load or a support.
Rise onto your toes and drive your knees forward.
Let hips drop slightly behind as you sink deep, torso upright.
Push through the balls of your feet back to standing.
cues: Keep weight on the forefoot and knees forward.
Use a slow, controlled lowering phase.

mistakes.text: Sitting the hips straight back like a box squat.
mistakes.fix: Keep weight on the forefoot and drive the knees forward.

mistakes.text: Bouncing at the bottom with no control.
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly and control the bottom position.

spanish-squat.title: Spanish Squat
spanish-squat.about: A band behind the knees lets you sit back with a vertical shin, loading the quads with little knee stress.
steps: Loop a heavy band around a rack and behind both knees.
Step back until the band is taut and stand tall.
Sit back and down, keeping shins vertical against the band.
Lower to about parallel, then drive back up.
cues: Lean into the band and keep the torso upright.
Hold the bottom briefly to build quad tension.

mistakes.text: Letting the band slacken so knees drift forward.
mistakes.fix: Keep the band taut and your shins vertical against it.

mistakes.text: Rounding the back as you sit down.
mistakes.fix: Keep the torso upright as you sit back and down.

split-squat.title: Split Squat
split-squat.about: A stationary lunge that trains each leg alone, building quads and glutes and fixing side-to-side gaps.
steps: Stand in a long split stance, feet hip-width apart.
Hold the load and keep your torso tall.
Drop the back knee straight down toward the floor.
Push through the front foot to rise, then repeat.
cues: Let the front knee travel forward for more quad work.
Keep most of your weight on the front leg.

mistakes.text: Standing with feet on one line, which ruins balance.
mistakes.fix: Set your feet hip-width apart in a long split stance.

mistakes.text: Pushing off the back foot instead of the front.
