mistakes.fix: Keep most of your weight on the front leg and push through it.

bulgarian-split-squat.title: Bulgarian Split Squat
bulgarian-split-squat.about: Rear foot elevated split squat that gives a deep stretch on the front leg's glutes and quads.
steps: Place your back foot on a bench behind you.
Set the front foot far enough forward to sink deep.
Lower until the back knee nearly touches the floor.
Drive through the front foot to stand back up.
cues: Lean forward to bias glutes; stay upright to bias quads.
Control the descent and pause briefly in the stretch.

mistakes.text: Front foot too close, causing the heel to lift.
mistakes.fix: Set the front foot far enough forward to keep the heel down.

mistakes.text: Pushing mostly with the back leg.
mistakes.fix: Drive through the front foot to stand back up.

reverse-lunge.title: Reverse Lunge
reverse-lunge.about: Stepping backward keeps the front shin stable and knee-friendly while hitting quads and glutes hard.
steps: Stand tall holding the load.
Step one foot back and lower the back knee toward the floor.
Sink until the front thigh is about parallel or lower.
Drive through the front foot to return to standing.
cues: Keep the front heel planted throughout.
Short torso lean forward adds glute work.

mistakes.text: Stepping too short so the front knee jams forward.
mistakes.fix: Step back far enough to keep the front heel planted.

mistakes.text: Slamming the back knee into the floor.
mistakes.fix: Lower the back knee toward the floor under control.

walking-lunge.title: Walking Lunge
walking-lunge.about: Continuous forward lunges that build leg size, single-leg strength and conditioning at once.
steps: Stand tall, holding weights at your sides if used.
Step forward and lower the back knee toward the floor.
Drive through the front foot and bring the back leg through.
Step straight into the next lunge and keep walking.
cues: Short steps bias quads; long steps bias glutes.
Keep hips square and core braced.

mistakes.text: Letting the front knee cave inward.
mistakes.fix: Keep the front knee in line with the toes and hips square.

mistakes.text: Rushing reps and cutting the depth.
mistakes.fix: Lower the back knee toward the floor on every step.

lateral-lunge.title: Lateral Lunge
lateral-lunge.about: A side-to-side lunge that stretches and strengthens the adductors while working glutes and quads.
steps: Stand with feet together, holding the weight at your chest.
Step or slide one leg out wide to the side.
Sit back into the working hip, keeping the other leg straight.
Push through the bent leg to return to the start.
cues: Keep your chest up and the heel of the bent leg down.
Feel the stretch along the inner thigh of the straight leg.

mistakes.text: Letting the bent knee cave inward.
mistakes.fix: Keep the bent knee in line with your toes.

mistakes.text: Rounding the back to reach lower.
mistakes.fix: Keep your chest up and sit back into the working hip.

step-up.title: Step-Up
step-up.about: A single-leg move onto a box that builds quads and glutes with very little lower-back load.
steps: Stand facing a box or bench at about knee height.
Place one whole foot firmly on top.
Drive through that foot to stand up on the box.
Lower slowly with control back to the floor.
cues: Minimize push-off from the bottom foot.
Lower slowly; the eccentric matters as much as the lift.

mistakes.text: Bouncing off the floor leg to cheat the rep.
mistakes.fix: Drive through the top foot and minimize push-off from below.

mistakes.text: Letting the working knee collapse inward.
mistakes.fix: Keep the working knee in line with your toes.

sumo-squat.title: Sumo Squat
sumo-squat.about: A wide-stance squat that shifts work toward the adductors and glutes.
steps: Stand wide with toes turned out about 30–45 degrees.
Hold one dumbbell vertically between your legs.
Sit straight down, pushing knees out over the toes.
Reach a deep stretch, then stand by squeezing glutes.
cues: Keep the torso upright and chest proud.
Stand on a step to let the weight go deeper.

mistakes.text: Knees collapsing inward past the toes.
mistakes.fix: Push your knees out over your toes.

mistakes.text: Turning it into a hip hinge with a rounded back.
mistakes.fix: Sit straight down with the torso upright and chest proud.

single-leg-squat.title: Single Leg Squat
single-leg-squat.about: Squatting on one leg builds quad and glute strength, balance and knee control with light loads.
steps: Stand on one leg, holding a support if needed.
Extend or tuck the free leg out of the way.
Sit down slowly on the working leg as deep as you control.
Drive through the whole foot to stand back up.
cues: Keep the working knee tracking over the toes.
Use support only as much as you need.

mistakes.text: Dropping into the bottom without control.
mistakes.fix: Sit down slowly, only as deep as you control.

mistakes.text: Twisting the hips to escape the hard part.
mistakes.fix: Keep hips level and the knee tracking over the toes.

quad-stretch.title: Quad Stretch
quad-stretch.about: A mobility drill that lengthens the quads and hip flexors to improve recovery and range of motion.
steps: Stand tall and hold a support for balance.
Bend one knee and grab the ankle behind you.
Pull the heel toward your glutes and hold 2 seconds.
Release, repeat for the set reps, then switch legs.
cues: Tuck your pelvis under to feel the stretch higher on the thigh.
Keep knees close together.

mistakes.text: Arching the lower back instead of stretching the quad.
mistakes.fix: Tuck your pelvis under and keep the knees close together.

mistakes.text: Yanking the foot hard into pain.
mistakes.fix: Pull the heel gently toward your glutes, never into pain.

cardio.title: Cardio
cardio.about: Steady movement that raises heart rate to build aerobic fitness and help recovery between sessions.
steps: Pick a mode such as walking, cycling, rowing or a sport.
Warm up for a few minutes at an easy pace.
Keep moving at the target effort for the set time or distance.
Cool down gradually before stopping.
cues: Most sessions should allow you to hold a conversation.
Breathe steadily and stay relaxed.

mistakes.text: Going all-out every session and hurting leg recovery.
mistakes.fix: Keep most sessions at a pace where you can hold a conversation.

mistakes.text: Skipping the warm-up.
mistakes.fix: Warm up for a few minutes at an easy pace first.

tuck-jump.title: Tuck Jump
tuck-jump.about: An explosive jump bringing knees to chest, building power, hip-flexor and core strength and conditioning.
steps: Stand on a cushioned surface, feet hip-width apart.
Dip into a half squat and swing your arms.
Explode up and pull your knees toward your chest.
Land softly on the balls of your feet and jump again.
cues: Land quietly with bent knees.
Exhale as you jump, inhale on the way down.

mistakes.text: Landing stiff-legged on your heels.
mistakes.fix: Land softly on the balls of your feet with bent knees.

mistakes.text: Losing height as you fatigue instead of resting.
mistakes.fix: Rest when your jump height starts to drop.

nordic-curl.title: Nordic Curl
nordic-curl.about: A bodyweight eccentric that overloads the hamstrings at long lengths; strong evidence for growth and injury prevention.
steps: Kneel on a pad with your ankles anchored.
Keep a straight line from knees to head, hips extended.
Lower your body forward as slowly as you can.
Catch yourself with your hands, then pull or push back up.
cues: Squeeze glutes so you hinge at the knee, not the hip.
Fight gravity all the way down.

mistakes.text: Bending at the hips to shorten the lever.
mistakes.fix: Squeeze glutes to keep a straight line from knees to head.

mistakes.text: Dropping quickly through the hardest range.
mistakes.fix: Lower as slowly as you can, fighting gravity all the way down.

lying-leg-curl.title: Lying Leg Curl
lying-leg-curl.about: Isolates the hamstrings through knee flexion, covering the muscle that hinges train less.
steps: Lie face down with knees just off the bench edge.
Set the pad just above your heels.
Curl your heels toward your glutes as far as possible.
Lower slowly until your legs are almost straight.
cues: Press hips into the pad so they don't lift.
Control a 2–3 second eccentric.

mistakes.text: Hips rising off the bench to swing the weight.
mistakes.fix: Press your hips into the pad for every rep.

mistakes.text: Cutting the stretched, straight-leg part of the rep.
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly until your legs are almost straight.

seated-leg-curl.title: Seated Leg Curl
seated-leg-curl.about: Flexed hips put the hamstrings on stretch, making this among the best leg curls for growth.
steps: Sit with knees aligned to the machine's pivot.
Lock the thigh pad down firmly above your knees.
Curl your heels down and back as far as possible.
Return slowly until your legs are fully extended.
cues: Lean your torso forward for a bigger hamstring stretch.
Squeeze hard at full flexion.

mistakes.text: Leaving the thigh pad loose so you slide around.
mistakes.fix: Lock the thigh pad down firmly above your knees.

mistakes.text: Letting the weight snap back up.
mistakes.fix: Return slowly until your legs are fully extended.

dumbbell-leg-curl.title: Dumbbell Leg Curl
dumbbell-leg-curl.about: A home-friendly leg curl using a dumbbell between the feet to isolate the hamstrings.
steps: Lie face down (or kneel) and grip a dumbbell between your feet.
Start with legs nearly straight.
Curl your heels toward your glutes.
Lower slowly, stopping before the dumbbell can slip.
cues: Squeeze the dumbbell tightly with your feet.
Keep hips pinned down throughout.

mistakes.text: Curling past vertical, where tension drops to zero.
mistakes.fix: Stop the curl before your shins pass vertical.

mistakes.text: Using too heavy a dumbbell to control safely.
mistakes.fix: Use a dumbbell light enough to grip and control safely.

ball-hamstring-curl.title: Ball Hamstring Curl
ball-hamstring-curl.about: A stability-ball curl that trains the hamstrings while the glutes hold your hips up.
steps: Lie on your back with heels on a stability ball.
Lift your hips into a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Curl the ball toward your glutes, keeping hips high.
Roll it back out slowly until legs are straight.
cues: Keep hips up throughout the set.
Move slowly to keep the ball stable.

mistakes.text: Letting the hips sag as you curl.
mistakes.fix: Keep your hips high throughout the set.

mistakes.text: Rushing and losing control of the ball.
mistakes.fix: Move slowly to keep the ball stable.

romanian-deadlift.title: Romanian Deadlift / Stiff Leg
romanian-deadlift.about: A hip hinge that loads the hamstrings and glutes in a deep stretch, a top hamstring builder.
steps: Stand tall holding the weight in front of your thighs.
Soften the knees slightly and keep them fixed.
Push your hips back, sliding the weight down your legs.
Stop at a deep hamstring stretch with a flat back, then drive hips forward.
cues: Think hips back, not chest down.
Keep the weight close to your legs.

mistakes.text: Rounding the lower back to reach lower.
mistakes.fix: Keep a flat back and stop at a deep hamstring stretch.

mistakes.text: Bending the knees so it becomes a squat.
mistakes.fix: Keep the knees softly bent and fixed; push the hips back.

glute-rdl.title: Glute-Biased RDL
glute-rdl.about: An RDL variant with more knee bend, rounded upper back or staggered stance to bias the glutes.
steps: Hold the weight and set a staggered or hip-width stance.
Bend the knees a bit more than a normal RDL.
Hinge forward, letting the upper back round slightly while hips go back.
Drive the hips through and squeeze the glutes at the top.
cues: Push the hips back until you feel a deep glute stretch.
Keep the lower back neutral even if the upper back rounds.

mistakes.text: Rounding the lower back under load.
mistakes.fix: Keep the lower back neutral, even if the upper back rounds.

mistakes.text: Hyperextending the spine at lockout instead of squeezing glutes.
mistakes.fix: Finish by squeezing the glutes, not by leaning back.

single-leg-rdl.title: Single Leg RDL
single-leg-rdl.about: A one-leg hinge that stretches the hamstrings and glutes and trains hip stability.
steps: Stand on one leg with a slight knee bend.
Hold the weight in one hand.
Hinge forward as the free leg extends behind you.
Lower to a deep stretch, then drive the hip forward to stand.
cues: Keep hips square to the floor.
Use a light support if balance limits you.

mistakes.text: Opening the hip so the pelvis rotates up.
mistakes.fix: Keep your hips square to the floor.

mistakes.text: Rounding the back to reach lower.
mistakes.fix: Keep a flat back and stop at a deep stretch.

hamstring-hyper.title: Hamstring Hyperextension
hamstring-hyper.about: A 45-degree back extension done as a hip hinge with a flat back, targeting the hamstrings.
steps: Set the pad just below your hip crease.
Hook your heels and keep a neutral spine.
Hinge at the hips and lower until you feel a strong hamstring stretch.
Drive hips into the pad to return to a straight line.
cues: Keep the back flat; move only at the hips.
Push heels into the footplate to feel the hamstrings.

mistakes.text: Rounding and unrounding the spine instead of hinging.
mistakes.fix: Keep the back flat and move only at the hips.

mistakes.text: Arching past straight at the top.
mistakes.fix: Stop when your body forms a straight line.

glute-hyper.title: Glute Hyperextension
glute-hyper.about: A back extension with rounded upper back and toes out that shifts work to the glutes.
steps: Set the pad lower on your thighs so hips can flex freely.
Turn toes out and round your upper back slightly.
Lower your torso toward the floor under control.
Squeeze the glutes to drive hips into the pad and rise.
cues: Think of pushing hips forward, not lifting with the back.
Pause and squeeze at the top.

mistakes.text: Driving the movement from the lower back.
mistakes.fix: Squeeze the glutes to drive your hips into the pad.

mistakes.text: Swinging up with momentum.
mistakes.fix: Lower under control and pause at the top.

hip-thrust.title: Hip Thrust
hip-thrust.about: Loads the glutes hardest at full hip extension, a great complement to squats and RDLs.
steps: Sit with your upper back against a bench, bar over your hips.
Plant feet so shins are vertical at the top.
Drive through your heels and lift hips until the torso is level.
Squeeze glutes, then lower under control.
cues: Tuck chin and ribs down; tilt the pelvis slightly back at the top.
Pause one second at lockout.

mistakes.text: Arching the lower back to fake lockout.
mistakes.fix: Keep chin and ribs down and stop when the torso is level.

mistakes.text: Feet too far out so hamstrings take over.
mistakes.fix: Plant your feet so shins are vertical at the top.

hip-abduction.title: Hip Abduction
hip-abduction.about: Isolates the upper glutes (glute medius and upper glute max) by pushing the legs apart.
steps: Sit in the machine with pads on the outside of your knees.
Lean forward slightly to bias the upper glute max.
Push your knees out as far as possible.
Return slowly until you feel a stretch on the outer hips.
cues: Use the full range, including the stretched start.
Keep a steady tempo; avoid bouncing the stack.

mistakes.text: Doing tiny partial reps with excessive weight.
mistakes.fix: Use a weight that lets you work the full range.

mistakes.text: Letting the weight slam back together.
mistakes.fix: Return slowly until you feel a stretch on the outer hips.

cable-kickback.title: Cable Glute Kickback
cable-kickback.about: A cable hip extension that isolates the glutes one side at a time.
steps: Attach an ankle cuff and face the cable stack.
Hinge forward slightly and hold the frame for support.
Kick the leg back and slightly out, squeezing the glute.
Return slowly until the hip is flexed and stretched.
cues: Move from the hip, not the lower back.
Keep the torso still and core braced.

mistakes.text: Arching the lower back to swing the leg higher.
mistakes.fix: Keep the core braced and move only from the hip.

mistakes.text: Rushing reps with no stretch at the front.
mistakes.fix: Return slowly until the hip is flexed and stretched.

rear-delt-fly.title: Rear Delt Fly / Raise
rear-delt-fly.about: Isolates the rear delts by moving the arms out and back, improving shoulder balance and posture.
steps: Lie chest-down on an incline bench or sit facing the machine.
Hold the weights or handles with arms nearly straight.
Sweep the arms out and back in a wide arc.
Pause, then return slowly to a full stretch.
cues: Lead with the elbows and keep shoulders down.
Use light weight and feel the back of the shoulder.

mistakes.text: Squeezing the shoulder blades so the traps take over.
mistakes.fix: Lead with the elbows and keep shoulders down.

mistakes.text: Swinging the torso to move heavier weight.
mistakes.fix: Use light weight and keep the torso still.

hip-adduction.title: Hip Adduction
hip-adduction.about: Isolates the inner-thigh adductors, which aid squat strength and hip health.
steps: Sit in the machine with pads on the inside of your knees.
Open the legs to a comfortable deep stretch.
Squeeze your knees together until the pads meet.
Return slowly to the stretched position.
cues: Lean slightly forward and sit tall.
Control the opening; the stretch drives growth.

mistakes.text: Starting with a range so wide it strains the groin.
mistakes.fix: Open only to a comfortable deep stretch.

mistakes.text: Letting the weight fling the legs open.
mistakes.fix: Control the opening and return slowly.

standing-calf-raise.title: Standing Calf Raise
standing-calf-raise.about: Straight-knee calf raises train both the gastrocnemius and soleus, best with a deep stretch at the bottom.
steps: Stand with the balls of your feet on a step or block.
Keep knees straight but not locked.
Lower your heels as far as possible and pause in the stretch.
Rise onto your big toe as high as you can, then lower slowly.
cues: Pause 1–2 seconds at the bottom to kill the bounce.
Push through the big toe, not the outer foot.

mistakes.text: Bouncing quick half reps off the Achilles tendon.
mistakes.fix: Pause 1–2 seconds in the bottom stretch each rep.

mistakes.text: Bending the knees to help push the weight.
mistakes.fix: Keep knees straight but not locked.

leg-press-calf-raise.title: Leg Press Calf Raise
leg-press-calf-raise.about: Uses the leg press to load the calves heavily and safely through a full stretch.
steps: Sit in the leg press with the balls of your feet on the platform's lower edge.
Press the sled up with knees straight but soft.
Let the platform push your toes back into a deep stretch.
Press through the big toes to full ankle extension.
cues: Keep the safety handles within reach.
Pause at the bottom stretch each rep.

mistakes.text: Bending the knees to move the sled.
mistakes.fix: Keep knees straight but soft and move only at the ankle.

mistakes.text: Feet slipping too high so the range shrinks.
mistakes.fix: Keep the balls of your feet on the platform's lower edge.

seated-calf-raise.title: Seated Calf Raise
seated-calf-raise.about: Bent knees slacken the gastrocnemius so the soleus does most of the work.
steps: Sit with the pad snug across your lower thighs.
Place the balls of your feet on the platform edge.
Lower heels to a deep stretch and pause.
Drive up onto the big toes as high as possible.
cues: Use a full range; the deep stretch matters most.
Keep a controlled tempo with no bouncing.

mistakes.text: Short, bouncy reps that skip the stretch.
mistakes.fix: Lower heels to a deep stretch and pause each rep.

mistakes.text: Rocking the torso to lift the weight.
mistakes.fix: Keep the torso still and lift with your calves.

tibialis-raise.title: Tibialis Raise
tibialis-raise.about: Trains the tibialis anterior on the front of the shin, supporting knee and ankle health.
steps: Sit or lean with heels on a bench edge and the weight on your feet.
Let your toes drop down into a full stretch.
Pull your toes up toward your shins as high as possible.
Pause, then lower slowly.
cues: Keep the heel fixed; move only at the ankle.
Use high reps and chase a burn.

mistakes.text: Kicking the weight up from the knee.
mistakes.fix: Keep the heel fixed and move only at the ankle.

mistakes.text: Skipping the bottom stretch.
mistakes.fix: Let your toes drop into a full stretch each rep.

hanging-knee-raise.title: Hanging Knee Raise
hanging-knee-raise.about: Hanging and curling the pelvis up trains the lower abs and grip with no equipment beyond a bar.
steps: Hang from a bar or straps with arms straight.
Brace your core and stop any swing.
Raise your knees toward your chest, curling the pelvis up.
Lower slowly until legs are straight below you.
cues: Think of tilting the pelvis up, not just lifting the knees.
Exhale as you raise.

mistakes.text: Swinging the body for momentum.
mistakes.fix: Brace your core and stop any swing before each rep.

mistakes.text: Only lifting knees to hip height without pelvic curl.
mistakes.fix: Curl the pelvis up as the knees rise toward your chest.

reverse-crunch.title: Reverse Crunch / Lying Leg Raise
reverse-crunch.about: Curling the pelvis toward the ribs on a bench targets the lower abs.
steps: Lie on a flat or decline bench and grip behind your head.
Bend or straighten the legs, lifted off the bench.
Curl the pelvis up so the hips lift off the bench.
Lower slowly until legs are nearly flat.
cues: Keep the lower back pressed down at the start.
Move slowly; the curl is small but intense.

mistakes.text: Swinging the legs with no pelvic curl.
mistakes.fix: Curl the pelvis up so the hips lift off the bench.

mistakes.text: Arching the lower back as the legs lower.
mistakes.fix: Keep the lower back pressed down as the legs lower.

crunch.title: Crunch
crunch.about: Spinal flexion with the rib cage curling toward the pelvis directly trains the rectus abdominis.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent or feet elevated.
Hold the weight on your chest or arms forward.
Curl your ribs toward your pelvis, lifting the shoulder blades.
Lower slowly until your upper back touches down.
cues: Think of rolling the spine up, not lifting with the neck.
Exhale fully at the top.

mistakes.text: Yanking on the head with the hands.
mistakes.fix: Rest your hands lightly and roll the spine up with your abs.

mistakes.text: Lifting with the hip flexors into a sit-up.
mistakes.fix: Curl your ribs toward your pelvis, lifting only the shoulder blades.

decline-crunch.title: Decline Crunch / Sit-Up
decline-crunch.about: The decline adds resistance and a deeper stretch for the abs at the bottom.
steps: Lock your feet under the pads of a decline bench.
Lie back with arms crossed or overhead.
Curl your torso up, rounding the spine segment by segment.
Lower slowly, letting the abs stretch at the bottom.
cues: Round the spine instead of hinging at the hips.
Control the lowering for a 2–3 second eccentric.

mistakes.text: Flopping down without control.
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly with a 2–3 second eccentric.

mistakes.text: Pulling up with the hip flexors and a flat back.
mistakes.fix: Round the spine segment by segment instead of hinging at the hips.

cable-crunch.title: Cable / Machine Crunch
cable-crunch.about: A loadable crunch that lets you progressively overload the abs like any other muscle.
steps: Kneel facing a cable with a rope, or sit in the crunch machine.
Hold the handles by your head and fix your hips in place.
Crunch your ribs toward your pelvis, rounding the spine.
Return slowly until your abs are fully stretched.
cues: Keep hips still; the spine does the bending.
Exhale hard at full contraction.

mistakes.text: Sitting back on the heels so the hips do the work.
mistakes.fix: Keep your hips fixed; let the spine do the bending.

mistakes.text: Pulling with the arms instead of the abs.
mistakes.fix: Hold the handles by your head and crunch with your abs.

ab-rollout.title: Ab Rollout
ab-rollout.about: An anti-extension move that loads the abs in a long, stretched position.
steps: Kneel holding a barbell or ab wheel under your shoulders.
Brace and tuck your pelvis slightly.
Roll forward slowly as far as you can without arching.
Pull back with your abs to the start.
cues: Keep a slight hollow; ribs down.
Only go as far as you can keep the back flat.

mistakes.text: Letting the lower back sag at full extension.
mistakes.fix: Roll out only as far as you can keep the back flat.

mistakes.text: Pulling back with the hips first.
mistakes.fix: Pull back with your abs, keeping ribs down.

v-up.title: V-Up
v-up.about: Raises the torso and legs together, training upper and lower abs in one move.
steps: Lie flat with arms overhead and legs straight.
Brace and press your lower back down.
Lift arms and legs together, reaching hands toward feet.
Lower both slowly back to just above the floor.
cues: Curl the spine; don't just hinge at the hips.
Bend the knees if you can't keep legs straight.

mistakes.text: Flopping back down with no control.
mistakes.fix: Lower arms and legs slowly to just above the floor.

mistakes.text: Arching the lower back at the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Keep your lower back pressed down; bend the knees if needed.

seated-bicycle.title: Seated Bicycle
seated-bicycle.about: A seated twisting crunch that trains the obliques and lower abs together.
steps: Sit on the floor, lean back slightly and lift your feet.
Place hands lightly behind your head.
Bring one knee in while rotating the opposite elbow toward it.
Switch sides in a smooth pedaling rhythm.
cues: Rotate through the ribs, not just the elbows.
Keep the movement slow and controlled.

mistakes.text: Pulling on the neck.
mistakes.fix: Keep your hands light behind your head and rotate through the ribs.

mistakes.text: Racing through reps with tiny rotation.
mistakes.fix: Slow down and rotate fully through the ribs on each side.

dumbbell-lateral-raise.title: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
dumbbell-lateral-raise.about: Isolates the side delts, the key muscle for wider-looking shoulders.
steps: Stand or sit tall holding dumbbells at your sides, palms facing in.
Lean slightly forward and keep a soft bend in the elbows.
Raise the dumbbells out to the sides until your arms are about parallel to the floor.
Lower slowly under control until your arms are nearly at your sides.
cues: Lead with the elbows, as if pushing the weights out toward the walls.
Keep the shoulders down, away from the ears.
Take 2–3 seconds on the way down.

mistakes.text: Swinging the torso to heave the weight up.
mistakes.fix: Keep the torso still and lead with the elbows.

mistakes.text: Shrugging so the upper traps take over the lift.
mistakes.fix: Keep the shoulders down, away from the ears.

incline-lateral-raise.title: Incline Dumbbell Lateral Raise
incline-lateral-raise.about: Loads the side delt hardest near the bottom, where it is stretched.
steps: Set a bench to a moderate incline and lie on it as cued, braced and stable.
Let the working arm hang down with a slight elbow bend.
Raise the dumbbell out and up until the arm is roughly in line with your shoulder.
Lower slowly back to the deep stretched position.
cues: Keep the arm moving out to the side, not forward.
Own the bottom stretch; do not let the weight bounce.
Stop before the shoulder starts to shrug.

mistakes.text: Cutting the bottom of the range short.
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly all the way back to the deep stretched position.

mistakes.text: Using a weight so heavy the torso rolls to help.
mistakes.fix: Use a weight you can lift while staying braced and stable.

cable-lateral-raise.title: Cable Lateral Raise
cable-lateral-raise.about: Keeps constant tension on the side delts, especially in the stretched bottom range.
steps: Set the pulley low and grab the handle with the arm across your body.
Stand tall, brace, and keep a slight bend in the elbow.
Sweep the arm out and up until it is about shoulder height.
Return slowly, letting the cable pull the arm across your body.
cues: Think of moving the elbow out, not lifting the hand.
Keep the shoulder blade down and stable.
Pause briefly at the top before a slow lowering.

mistakes.text: Leaning away and using the body to move the weight.
mistakes.fix: Stand tall, brace, and move only the arm.

mistakes.text: Letting the stack slam between reps and losing tension.
mistakes.fix: Return slowly and keep the cable taut between reps.

y-raise.title: Y Raise
y-raise.about: Trains the side delts and lower traps together, building healthy overhead shoulder control.
steps: Set up (bench, cable or TRX) with arms hanging in front of you.
Point thumbs up and keep the elbows almost straight.
Raise your arms up and out into a Y shape, about 30 degrees from your head.
Lower slowly back to the start.
cues: Pull the shoulder blades slightly back and down as you lift.
Use light weight and feel the delts, not the neck.
Keep the ribs down; do not arch the lower back.

mistakes.text: Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears.
mistakes.fix: Pull the shoulder blades slightly back and down as you lift.

mistakes.text: Arching the back to get the arms higher.
mistakes.fix: Keep the ribs down and raise only as high as you can without arching.

w-raise.title: Incline Dumbbell W Raise
w-raise.about: Targets the rear delts, rotator cuff and mid traps for balanced, healthy shoulders.
steps: Lie chest-down on an incline bench holding light dumbbells.
Bend the elbows to about 90 degrees, close to your sides.
Pull the elbows back while rotating the forearms up into a W shape.
Squeeze briefly, then lower slowly.
cues: Keep the chest glued to the bench.
Rotate the hands up and back, elbows staying bent.
Move slowly with light weight.

mistakes.text: Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears.
mistakes.fix: Keep shoulders down and pull the elbows back.

mistakes.text: Lifting the chest off the pad to cheat the reps.
mistakes.fix: Keep the chest glued to the bench with light weight.

bus-driver.title: Bus Driver
bus-driver.about: Works the front delts isometrically while rotating the shoulder, building endurance and control.
steps: Hold a plate (or dumbbell) with both hands at arm's length in front of you.
Raise it to about shoulder height with elbows nearly straight.
Rotate the plate side to side like turning a steering wheel.
Keep the arms at height for the whole set, then lower slowly.
cues: Keep the plate at shoulder level without dropping.
Brace the core so the torso stays still.
Move the rotation slowly and fully.

mistakes.text: Leaning back to hold the weight up.
mistakes.fix: Brace the core so the torso stays still and upright.

mistakes.text: Letting the arms sink as fatigue sets in.
mistakes.fix: Keep the plate at shoulder level for the whole set.

front-raise.title: Front Raise
front-raise.about: Isolates the front delts with a simple shoulder-flexion movement.
steps: Hold the weight in front of your thighs with arms nearly straight.
Brace your core and stand tall.
Raise the weight forward and up to about eye level.
Lower slowly back to your thighs.
cues: Keep the torso still; the arms do the work.
Lift with the shoulders, not by leaning back.
Control the lowering for 2–3 seconds.

mistakes.text: Swinging the weight up with the hips.
mistakes.fix: Brace your core and keep the torso still; the arms do the work.

mistakes.text: Lifting far above the head and shrugging.
mistakes.fix: Stop at about eye level with shoulders down.

arnold-rotation.title: Arnold Rotation
arnold-rotation.about: Rotates the arms through the front-to-side delt range, hitting multiple delt heads.
steps: Hold dumbbells at shoulder height, palms facing you, elbows in front.
Rotate the elbows out to the sides while turning the palms forward.
Stop with elbows wide and dumbbells beside your head, without pressing.
Reverse slowly back to the start position.
cues: Keep tension on the delts through the whole arc.
Move the elbows, keeping forearms roughly vertical.
Use slow, deliberate reps.

mistakes.text: Turning it into a fast, jerky press.
mistakes.fix: Use slow, deliberate reps through the whole arc.

mistakes.text: Arching the lower back to move heavier weight.
mistakes.fix: Use a lighter weight and keep your back neutral.

front-delt-around-the-world.title: Incline Front Delt Around The World
front-delt-around-the-world.about: Takes the front delts through a long overhead arc for a big range of motion.
steps: Lie back on an incline bench holding light dumbbells at your hips.
Keep the elbows slightly bent and palms facing up.
Sweep the arms out and up in a wide arc until overhead.
Reverse the arc slowly back down to your hips.
cues: Keep the lower back on the bench.
Move in one smooth, wide circle.
Use light weight to protect the shoulder joint.

mistakes.text: Bending the elbows and turning it into a press.
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows slightly bent and fixed through the circle.

mistakes.text: Going heavy and losing control overhead.
mistakes.fix: Use light weight and move in one smooth, wide circle.

barbell-overhead-press.title: Barbell Shoulder Press
barbell-overhead-press.about: A heavy compound press that builds front-delt and triceps strength and size.
steps: Grip the bar just outside shoulder width, resting it on the upper chest.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Press the bar up in a straight line, moving your head back slightly.
Lock out overhead, then lower under control to the upper chest.
cues: Keep the forearms vertical under the bar.
Ribs down; avoid excessive back arch.
Lower to full depth on every rep.

mistakes.text: Leaning back hard and turning it into an incline press.
mistakes.fix: Brace your core, squeeze your glutes and keep the ribs down.

mistakes.text: Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides.
mistakes.fix: Keep the forearms vertical under the bar.

dumbbell-shoulder-press.title: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
dumbbell-shoulder-press.about: Builds the front delts with a free path and a deep stretch at the bottom.
steps: Sit on a high-incline bench with dumbbells at shoulder height.
Plant your feet and keep your back against the pad.
Press the dumbbells up until your arms are nearly straight.
Lower slowly until the dumbbells reach shoulder level or slightly below.
cues: Keep the wrists stacked over the elbows.
Get a full stretch at the bottom of each rep.
Press up and slightly in, without clanging the weights.

mistakes.text: Stopping halfway down to lift heavier.
mistakes.fix: Lower to shoulder level or slightly below on every rep.

mistakes.text: Arching off the bench to finish reps.
mistakes.fix: Plant your feet and keep your back against the pad.

machine-shoulder-press.title: Machine Shoulder Press
machine-shoulder-press.about: A stable press that lets you train the front delts hard with less balance demand.
steps: Set the seat so the handles start at or just below shoulder height.
Sit with your back flat against the pad and grip the handles.
Press up until your arms are nearly locked out.
Lower slowly to the deepest comfortable stretch.
cues: Keep the shoulder blades against the pad.
Control every negative; no bouncing at the bottom.
Keep elbows slightly in front of the torso.

mistakes.text: Setting the seat too high and cutting the range.
mistakes.fix: Set the seat so the handles start at or just below shoulder height.

mistakes.text: Pushing the head forward and shrugging.
mistakes.fix: Keep your head back and shoulder blades against the pad.

smith-shoulder-press.title: Smith Machine Shoulder Press
smith-shoulder-press.about: A guided bar press that lets you overload the front delts safely.
steps: Place a bench under the Smith bar so the bar lowers to your upper chest.
Grip slightly wider than shoulders and unrack the bar.
Press up until your arms are nearly straight.
Lower slowly until the bar is around chin to upper-chest level.
cues: Keep forearms vertical at the bottom.
Keep your back on the pad and core braced.
Use the full range on every rep.

mistakes.text: Positioning the bench so the bar hits your face.
mistakes.fix: Place the bench so the bar lowers to your upper chest.

mistakes.text: Bouncing out of the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly and press up smoothly from the bottom.

viking-press.title: Viking Press
viking-press.about: A neutral-grip overhead press on an arc that is friendly to the shoulder joint.
steps: Stand facing the handles (or landmine end) with them at shoulder height.
Grip with palms facing each other and brace your core.
Press up and slightly forward until your arms are nearly straight.
Lower slowly back to shoulder level.
cues: Keep elbows tucked slightly forward.
Stack ribs over hips; do not lean back.
Control the lowering phase.

mistakes.text: Using leg drive to push the weight up.
mistakes.fix: Keep the legs still and press with the shoulders and arms.

mistakes.text: Cutting the bottom of the press short.
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly all the way back to shoulder level.

upright-row.title: Wide Grip Upright Row
upright-row.about: A wide grip shifts the upright row onto the side delts and upper traps.
steps: Grip the bar about 1.5 times shoulder width with an overhand grip.
Stand tall with the bar at arm's length against your thighs.
Pull the elbows up and out until they reach shoulder height.
Lower slowly until the arms are straight.
cues: Lead with the elbows; hands stay below them.
Stop at shoulder height to keep the shoulder comfortable.
Keep the bar close to the body.

mistakes.text: Using a narrow grip and pulling the bar to the chin.
mistakes.fix: Grip about 1.5 times shoulder width and stop at shoulder height.

mistakes.text: Jerking the weight up with the hips.
mistakes.fix: Stand tall and pull smoothly, leading with the elbows.

rear-delt-raise.title: Rear Delt Raise
rear-delt-raise.about: Isolates the rear delts, improving shoulder balance, posture and 3D shoulder look.
steps: Hinge forward or lie chest-down on an incline bench, arms hanging.
Hold the weights with a slight bend in the elbows.
Sweep the arms out and back until they are in line with your torso.
Lower slowly back to a full stretch.
cues: Think of pushing the weights out wide, not squeezing the shoulder blades.
Keep the neck neutral and the torso still.
Use light weight and controlled tempo.

mistakes.text: Rowing the weight with bent elbows so the back takes over.
mistakes.fix: Keep a slight, fixed elbow bend and push the weights out wide.

mistakes.text: Swinging the torso up to lift heavier.
mistakes.fix: Keep the torso still and use light weight.

rear-delt-cable-fly.title: Cable Rear Delt Fly
rear-delt-cable-fly.about: Cables keep the rear delts loaded through the full range, including the stretch.
steps: Set the pulley at or below shoulder height and grab the handle across your body.
Stand or sit tall with a slight bend in the elbow.
Sweep the arm out and back until it lines up with your torso.
Return slowly across the body to a full stretch.
cues: Keep the arm low and close to the body if cued.
Move from the shoulder; the elbow angle stays fixed.
Keep the shoulder blade quiet rather than retracting hard.

mistakes.text: Turning it into a row by bending the elbow.
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbow angle fixed and move from the shoulder.

mistakes.text: Rotating the torso to help the weight move.
mistakes.fix: Stand or sit tall and keep the torso still.

rear-delt-around-the-world.title: Rear Delt Around The World
rear-delt-around-the-world.about: Combines a rear-delt sweep with shoulder rotation for a long range of motion.
steps: Lie chest-down on an incline bench with light dumbbells hanging.
Raise the arms out to the sides with elbows slightly bent.
Continue the arc forward and overhead, or rotate as cued.
Reverse the path slowly back to the start.
cues: Keep the chest on the pad throughout.
Use a slow, smooth circle with light weight.
Feel the back of the shoulder, not the neck.

mistakes.text: Using too much weight and losing the arc.
mistakes.fix: Use light weight and keep a slow, smooth circle.

mistakes.text: Shrugging at the top of the circle.
mistakes.fix: Keep shoulders down and feel the back of the shoulder, not the neck.

landmine-rear-delt-raise.title: Landmine Rear Delt Raise
landmine-rear-delt-raise.about: The landmine arc gives the rear delt a strong stretch and steady resistance.
steps: Stand side-on to a landmine, hinge forward, and grab the bar end.
Let the arm hang across your body with a slight elbow bend.
Sweep the arm out and up until it lines up with your torso.
Lower slowly to the stretched position.
cues: Hand position (low, mid, high) changes the line of pull; stay consistent.
Keep the torso still and the neck neutral.
Lead with the back of the shoulder.

mistakes.text: Rotating the torso open to lift the bar.
mistakes.fix: Keep the torso still and lead with the back of the shoulder.

mistakes.text: Bending the elbow and rowing the weight.
mistakes.fix: Keep a slight, fixed elbow bend as you sweep the arm out.

behind-back-barbell-raise.title: Behind The Back Barbell Raise
behind-back-barbell-raise.about: Trains the rear delts through shoulder extension with the bar held behind you.
steps: Hold a barbell behind your hips with an overhand, shoulder-width grip.
Stand tall with arms straight and chest up.
Raise the bar back and away from your body using your shoulders.
Lower slowly until it lightly touches your hips.
cues: Keep the arms straight and the torso upright.
Move a short, strict range with no momentum.
Squeeze the back of the shoulders at the top.

mistakes.text: Leaning forward to make the bar travel higher.
mistakes.fix: Stay upright and move a short, strict range.

mistakes.text: Bending the elbows and shrugging.
mistakes.fix: Keep the arms straight and shoulders down.

machine-rear-delt-fly.title: Machine Rear Delt Fly
machine-rear-delt-fly.about: A stable reverse pec-deck that makes it easy to load the rear delts hard.
steps: Set the handles to the rear-delt position and the seat so arms are at shoulder height.
Sit facing the pad and grab the handles with a slight elbow bend.
Sweep the arms out and back until they line up with your torso.
Return slowly until you feel a stretch in the back of the shoulders.
cues: Push out wide with the hands rather than pinching the shoulder blades.
Keep your chest on the pad.
Control the stretch on every rep.

mistakes.text: Letting the weights slam and losing tension.
mistakes.fix: Return slowly and control the stretch on every rep.

mistakes.text: Leaning back off the pad to swing the weight.
mistakes.fix: Keep your chest on the pad for the whole set.

rear-delt-row.title: Rear Delt Row
rear-delt-row.about: A wide-elbow row that shifts the work from the lats onto the rear delts.
steps: Set up with a cable, machine or TRX, arms straight in front at chest height.
Use an overhand grip and raise the elbows out to about shoulder level.
Pull the elbows back and wide until they pass your torso.
Extend the arms slowly back to a full stretch.
cues: Keep the elbows high and flared, about 70–90 degrees.
Pull with the back of the shoulders, not the biceps.
Pause briefly at the end of each pull.

mistakes.text: Dropping the elbows so it becomes a lat row.
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows high and flared, about 70–90 degrees.

mistakes.text: Leaning back and using body momentum.
mistakes.fix: Keep the body still and pull with the back of the shoulders.

face-pull.title: Cable Face Pull
face-pull.about: Builds the rear delts and external rotators, great for shoulder health and posture.
steps: Set a rope at upper-chest to face height and grip it with thumbs toward you.
Step back until the arms are straight and the cable is taut.
Pull the rope toward your face, spreading the ends apart.
Finish with hands beside your ears, then return slowly.
cues: Keep elbows high, at or above the hands' line.
Rotate the hands back at the end of the pull.
Stay upright; do not lean back.

mistakes.text: Pulling to the chest with low elbows.
mistakes.fix: Keep elbows high and pull the rope toward your face.

mistakes.text: Using too much weight and yanking with the lower back.
mistakes.fix: Use a lighter weight and stay upright.

cable-rotation.title: Cable Rotation
cable-rotation.about: Trains the obliques and core to rotate powerfully and resist twisting.
steps: Set the cable at mid-height and stand side-on with feet shoulder-width.
Hold the handle with both hands, arms extended in front of your chest.
Rotate your torso away from the stack, keeping arms long.
Return slowly, then switch sides after the set.
cues: Turn from the ribcage while hips stay mostly square.
Keep the core braced throughout.
Control the return; do not let the cable yank you.

mistakes.text: Pulling with the arms instead of rotating the torso.
mistakes.fix: Keep the arms long and turn from the ribcage.

mistakes.text: Twisting fast and loose through the lower back.
mistakes.fix: Brace the core and rotate slowly under control.

shrug.title: Shrug
shrug.about: Directly builds the upper traps by elevating the shoulder blades under load.
steps: Hold the weight at arm's length with a firm grip.
Stand or sit tall and let the shoulders drop for a full stretch.
Shrug the shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Pause briefly, then lower slowly to the stretched position.
cues: Lift the shoulders up, not forward or in circles.
Keep the arms straight; do not bend the elbows.
Use straps if grip limits the set.

mistakes.text: Bouncing short reps without a full stretch at the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Let the shoulders drop for a full stretch before each shrug.

mistakes.text: Rolling the shoulders, which adds nothing but strain.
mistakes.fix: Shrug straight up toward your ears, then straight down.

incline-shrug.title: Incline Dumbbell Shrug
incline-shrug.about: Leaning forward shrugs the blades up and back, hitting upper and mid traps.
steps: Lie chest-down on an incline bench, or hinge forward, holding dumbbells.
Let the arms hang straight and the shoulder blades spread apart.
Shrug the shoulders up and back toward your ears.
Hold briefly, then lower slowly to a full stretch.
cues: Think 'shoulders to ears' along the line of your torso.
Keep the arms long; no rowing with the elbows.
Pause at the top of each rep.

mistakes.text: Turning the shrug into a row.
mistakes.fix: Keep the arms long and move only the shoulders.

mistakes.text: Lifting the chest off the bench to gain range.
mistakes.fix: Keep your chest on the bench throughout.

mid-trap-shrug.title: Bent Over Mid Trap Shrug (Kelso Shrug)
mid-trap-shrug.about: Retracts the shoulder blades from a bent position to target the mid traps and rhomboids.
steps: Hinge forward to about 45 degrees or more, holding the weight with straight arms.
Let the shoulder blades spread wide at the bottom.
Squeeze the shoulder blades back together without bending the elbows.
Hold one second, then let them spread slowly.
cues: Move only the shoulder blades; the arms are just hooks.
Keep a neutral spine and a stable hinge.
Use a full protraction-to-retraction range.

mistakes.text: Bending the elbows and turning it into a row.
mistakes.fix: Keep the arms straight and move only the shoulder blades.

mistakes.text: Rounding the lower back while hinged.
mistakes.fix: Keep a neutral spine and a stable hinge.

high-elbow-shrug.title: High Elbow Shrug
high-elbow-shrug.about: A tiny row with high elbows that isolates the mid and upper traps.
steps: Grip the handles with arms extended and elbows flared out high.
Let the shoulder blades reach forward for a full stretch.
Pull the shoulder blades back and slightly up, barely bending the elbows.
Pause, then let the blades travel forward slowly.
cues: Keep the elbows at roughly shoulder height.
Drive the movement from the shoulder blades, not the arms.
Hold the squeeze for a second.

mistakes.text: Pulling a full row with the arms.
mistakes.fix: Barely bend the elbows and drive with the shoulder blades.

mistakes.text: Shrugging straight up into the neck only.
mistakes.fix: Pull the shoulder blades back and only slightly up.

hanging-scapular-shrug.title: Pull-Up Shrug (Scapular Pull-Up)
hanging-scapular-shrug.about: Depresses the shoulder blades from a hang, training the lower traps and lats.
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with straight arms, adding weight if cued.
Let the shoulders rise up toward your ears for a full stretch.
Pull the shoulders down and away from your ears, lifting your body slightly.
Lower slowly back to a full dead hang.
cues: Keep the elbows straight the whole time.
Think 'shoulders into back pockets'.
Pause at the top of each rep.

mistakes.text: Bending the arms and doing a partial pull-up.
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows straight and move only the shoulders.

mistakes.text: Swinging or kipping to move.
mistakes.fix: Stay still and lower slowly to a full dead hang.

pulldown-scapular-shrug.title: Lat Pulldown Shrug
pulldown-scapular-shrug.about: Isolates scapular depression on the cable, hitting the lower traps and lats.
steps: Sit at a pulldown station and grip the bar or V-bar with straight arms.
Let the weight pull your shoulders up toward your ears.
Pull the shoulder blades down without bending the elbows.
Hold briefly, then let the shoulders rise slowly.
cues: Keep the arms straight; only the shoulders move.
Sit tall with a slight lean back at most.
Use a full up-and-down shoulder range.

mistakes.text: Bending the elbows into a mini pulldown.
mistakes.fix: Keep the arms straight; only the shoulders move.

mistakes.text: Leaning back to move more weight.
mistakes.fix: Sit tall with a slight lean back at most.

wrist-curl.title: Wrist Curl
wrist-curl.about: Isolates the forearm flexors for bigger forearms and a stronger grip.
steps: Sit and rest your forearms on your thighs or a bench, palms up.
Let the wrists extend back so the weight rolls toward your fingertips.
Curl the wrists up as high as possible, squeezing the forearms.
Lower slowly to a full stretch.
cues: Keep the forearms pinned; only the wrists move.
Use the full range, including the finger roll at the bottom.
Higher reps (12–20) work well here.

mistakes.text: Lifting the elbows or forearms to cheat the weight up.
mistakes.fix: Keep the forearms pinned; only the wrists move.

mistakes.text: Doing short, bouncy reps.
mistakes.fix: Use the full range, including the finger roll at the bottom.

wrist-extension.title: Wrist Extension
wrist-extension.about: Strengthens the forearm extensors, balancing grip work and protecting the elbows.
steps: Rest your forearms on your thighs or a bench, palms facing down.
Let the hands drop down for a stretch on top of the forearm.
Raise the backs of the hands up as far as possible.
Lower slowly to the stretched position.
cues: Keep the forearms still; move only at the wrist.
Use lighter weight than wrist curls.
Pause briefly at the top.

mistakes.text: Lifting the forearms off the support.
mistakes.fix: Keep the forearms on the support; move only at the wrist.

mistakes.text: Dropping the weight quickly on the way down.
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly to the stretched position.

forearm-drag-curl.title: Forearm Drag Curl
forearm-drag-curl.about: Dragging the weight up the body with an overhand or neutral grip hammers the brachioradialis.
steps: Hold the weight against your thighs with an overhand or neutral grip.
Pull the elbows back as you drag the weight up along your body.
Curl until the weight reaches your lower chest.
Slide it back down slowly, keeping contact with your body.
cues: Elbows travel back, not forward.
Keep the weight close to your torso the whole time.
Keep wrists firm and straight.

mistakes.text: Letting the elbows drift forward like a normal curl.
mistakes.fix: Pull the elbows back and keep the weight close to your torso.

mistakes.text: Leaning back to heave the weight.
mistakes.fix: Stand still and drag the weight up with your arms.

forearm-pronation.title: Forearm Pronation
forearm-pronation.about: Trains the pronator muscles that turn the palm down, supporting elbow health and grip.
steps: Rest your forearm on a bench or thigh with the hand past the edge.
Hold the dumbbell end or strap with the palm facing up.
Rotate the forearm to turn the palm down.
Rotate back slowly to the start.
cues: Keep the elbow still; the twist comes from the forearm.
Choke up or down on the handle to adjust difficulty.
Move slowly through the full rotation.

mistakes.text: Moving the whole arm or shoulder to rotate.
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbow still and twist from the forearm.

mistakes.text: Letting the weight flop over quickly.
mistakes.fix: Rotate slowly in both directions.

forearm-supination.title: Forearm Supination
forearm-supination.about: Trains the supinator and biceps' twisting role, turning the palm up against resistance.
steps: Rest your forearm on a bench or thigh with the hand past the edge.
Hold the dumbbell end or strap with the palm facing down.
Rotate the forearm to turn the palm up.
Rotate back slowly to the start.
cues: Keep the elbow fixed at your side or on the support.
Use a light load and a full twist.
Control both directions.

mistakes.text: Swinging the arm to finish the rotation.
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbow fixed at your side or on the support.

mistakes.text: Going too heavy and shortening the range.
mistakes.fix: Use a light load and a full twist.

dead-hang.title: Dead Hang
dead-hang.about: Builds grip endurance and decompresses the shoulders through a long overhead hang.
steps: Grip a pull-up bar with hands about shoulder-width apart.
Lift your feet and hang with arms fully straight.
Keep a light brace in your core and breathe steadily.
Hold for the target time, then step down under control.
cues: Squeeze the bar hard throughout.
Let the shoulders stretch but avoid total slack.
Stay still; no swinging.

mistakes.text: Bending the arms to make the hang easier.
mistakes.fix: Keep your arms fully straight for the whole hang.

mistakes.text: Holding your breath during the hang.
mistakes.fix: Keep a light core brace and breathe steadily.

notes.seated-rear-delt-partial-raise: Partials: work only the stretched lower half of the range, ideally after full-range reps fail.
notes.seated-supinated-shrugs-garage-program: Palms facing forward (supinated) while seated; some lifters feel the traps better this way.
notes.side-lateral-buffet-bottom-garage-progra: Buffet (bottom): do partial reps in the lower, stretched portion of the range.
notes.side-lateral-buffet-full-rom-garage-prog: Buffet (full ROM): finish the sequence with full-range reps.
notes.side-lateral-buffet-top-garage-program: Buffet (top): do partial reps in the upper, contracted portion of the range.
notes.side-laterals-fixed-elbow: Fixed elbow: lock the elbow at about 90 degrees so the arm moves as one short lever.
notes.single-arm-bench-stabilized-dumbbell-sid: Hold a bench with the free hand to lock the torso and isolate the side delt.
notes.single-arm-cable-rear-delt-copy: Arms close to body: keep the cable path low beside the torso for a deep stretch.
notes.single-arm-cable-rear-delt-partials-copy: Single arm: train one side at a time for better focus and a stable torso.
notes.single-arm-dumbbell-rear-delt-raise-copy: Single arm: train one side at a time for better focus and a stable torso.
notes.single-arm-dumbbell-side-lateral-control: Single arm, controlled: one side at a time with a slow, strict tempo.
notes.single-arm-machine-rear-delt-fly-exagger: Single arm, reaching across the body at the bottom for an exaggerated stretch.
notes.single-arm-machine-shoulder-press-ryan_h: Single arm: train one side at a time for better focus and a stable torso.
notes.single-arm-rear-delt-db-raises: Single arm: train one side at a time for better focus and a stable torso.
notes.single-arm-side-lateral-machine-rear-del: Use a lateral raise machine facing the pad, one arm at a time, to train the rear delt.
notes.slight-incline-cable-straight-bar-revers: Lie back on a slight incline facing away from the cable for extra stretch.
notes.slight-incline-rear-delt-fixed-elbow-rot: Elbows fixed at 90 degrees on a slight incline; rotate the forearms up to hit rear delts and rotator cuff.
notes.slight-incline-rear-delt-raise: Slight incline partials: lie on a low incline and work the stretched part of the range.
notes.slightly-bent-dumbbell-shrugs: Only a slight forward lean, between a standing and a bent shrug.
notes.slow-motion-side-laterals-thumbs-up-gara: Super slow with thumbs pointing up, a slightly more front-delt-friendly hand position.
notes.smith-bent-over-mid-trap-shrugs: Smith machine: the fixed path lets you focus purely on squeezing.
notes.smith-shoulder-press-65-degree-scapular-: Set the bench to about 60 degrees and keep elbows in the scapular plane.
notes.smith-wide-grip-upright-row: Smith machine: the fixed bar path lets you focus purely on the delts.
notes.standing-dumbbell-straight-arm-partials: Straight-arm partials: elbows locked, reps only in the lower stretched range.
notes.strap-attachment-pronators: Cable strap attachment gives constant tension through the rotation.
notes.strap-attachment-supinator: Cable strap attachment gives constant tension through the rotation.
notes.supinated-barbell-front-raise-clusterfuc: Done lying chest-down on an incline bench so the torso cannot cheat.
Fixed elbow + cluster: elbows locked at 90 degrees, done in short mini-sets with brief rests.
notes.trx-rear-delt-pull-separate: TRX: pull with high elbows, then spread the arms wide at the top.
notes.trx-y-raise-ryan_humis514743: TRX: lean back on the straps and pull yourself up into a Y; walk feet forward to add difficulty.
notes.v-bar-lat-shrugs: Close neutral grip on a V-bar; think of driving the elbows toward your hips to feel the lats.
notes.v-bar-low-trap-shrugs: Lean back slightly and drive the shoulder blades down to bias the lower traps.
notes.v-bar-pull-up-shrugs: Hang from a V-bar with a close neutral grip.
notes.viking-press-neutral-grip: Neutral grip: palms facing each other for a more shoulder-friendly press.
notes.weighted-straight-hyper-drop-finish-copy: Focus on pulling the shoulders down to bias the lower traps.
notes.wide-grip-pull-up-shrugs-weighted: Weighted, wide grip; add load with a belt or dumbbell.
notes.wide-grip-smith-upright-row: Smith machine: the fixed bar path lets you focus purely on the delts.
